articleTitle: Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks (StackGAN) Text-to-Image Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Generating high quality images from textual description is an ongoing challenge which can have a wide range of practical uses. Some of such fields are computer vision, creation industry, e-commerce, education and many more. Currently existing text to image synthesizing techniques, while offering valuable insights still struggles to capture fine details and vivid object components that are crucial for real world application. We use an approach that uses Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks (StackGAN) to solve the problem of text-to-image generation. This includes using a two-stage process. In the first stage (Stage – 1 GAN), we aim to develop a system that is capable of generating the fundamental shape and color attributes of the object according to the text. In this stage, a low-resolution image is generation that is used as a foundation for the subsequent image refinement process. In the second stage (Stage – 2 GAN), we focus on enhancing the quality of image by incorporating the text descriptions and generating high-resolution image. This project aims to bridge the gap and advance the text-to-image generation to create images to create images that are textually accurate. By doing so, the project seeks to unlock the potential of this technology across various fields and bridge the gap between the power of language and art, design and content creation.

articleTitle: Automated Essay Scoring for IELTS using Classification and Regression Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The advancement of automated essay scoring (AES) mechanisms in the English proficiency evaluation through the standardized English proficiency tests like the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) is a hot subject these days. The purpose of this article, in particular, is to explore the application of regression and classification methods in both automated IELTS essay grading and customizing IELTS essay grades. Moreover, this study options classification and regression models to develop IELTS essay grading method by means of dataset of IELTS essays. The analysis employs methods to identify the linguistic and structural parts of essays, and also compares the model performance along with the baseline metrics. Automating the outcome provides a way for the grading process to eliminate human error and proves successful in assessing students’ IELTS essays with accuracy. With this study, a path brings to the light new directions for the research of ways to increase the effectiveness and consistency of language proficiency ES exam ratings, and a way to develop automatic evaluation systems.

articleTitle: SAriTA: A Generic Tool for Finding Rhetorical Figures in Indo-Aryan Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The paper presents SAriTA, a novel computational tool tailored for the identification of rhetorical figures, or Alankars, in Indo-Aryan languages. Designed to recognize 06 specific types of Alankars Checka Anupras (Type of alliteration) (CA), VratyaAnupras (Type of alliteration) (VA), AnantyaAnupras (Rhyme) (AA), Punurukti (Repetition) (PU), Upma (Simile) (Si), and Virodhabhas (Oxymoron) (Oy). SAriTA analyzes poetic texts across 15 different Indo-Aryan languages such as Angika (An), Bajjika (Ba), Bhojpuri (Bh), Brajbhasha (Br), Garhwali (Gr), Gujarati (Gj), Haryanvi (Hr), Hindi (Hi), Magahi (Mg), 1 (Mi), Marathi (Mr), Pali (Pa), Rajasthani (Rj ), Sanskrit (Sa), Sindhi (Sn),and one international language Nepali (Ne). By calculating the Percentage Error (PE) in identification, the tool evaluates its performance both language-wise and Alankar-wise, providing insights into its effectiveness and limitations. This research highlights the dependence of identification accuracy on both the algorithm and the inherent structure and stylistic elements of the poetry. After comparison with other Indo Aryan languages, it is observed that SAriTA performance is excel for Hindi and Maithili poetry.

articleTitle: Document Classification and Data Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: T- Data classification and extraction are fundamental tasks in the field of computer vision and data analysis. This abstract presents an overview of these concepts along with the utilization of Python and OpenCV, a popular computer vision library, in building data extraction tools. Data classification involves organizing data into categories or classes based on certain characteristics or features. It enables efficient data management and analysis by grouping similar data together. In the context of computer vision, data classification often involves categorizing images or videos based on their content, such as identifying objects, scenes, or patterns within them. Data extraction, on the other hand, involves retrieving specific information or features from a dataset. This process is crucial for tasks like data mining, information retrieval, and automated document processing. In computer vision applications, data extraction often entails locating and extracting relevant information from images or videos, such as text, objects, or numerical data.

articleTitle: Detection of AI-generated Text: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence is an important area in the computer science domain with a wide range of capabilities. With many people saying that they have encountered AI-generated content in the past years very few respondents feel confident in their ability to distinguish between real and fake content. This work aims to explore methods that effectively detect the content generated by AI. The investigation of the available online tools led to the determination of their limitations. Consequently, two separate algorithms were employed for detection and proper analysis: one is a classification-based approach that uses the Support Vector Machine (SVM) model for binary text classification, and the other is a statistical method that analyzes linguistic aspects to distinguish between writing generated by AI and humans. Both normal data, as well as rephrased data, were employed during the stress testing of these algorithms. The accuracy obtained on the raw dataset was very promising. The detection was 99.87% accurate. The accuracy rate of detecting rephrased texts reached 87.58% for the classification model and 84.91% for the statistical model. Additional analysis and observations were made regarding the ability of AI to generate text similar to humans.

articleTitle: Statistical Features based Content Based Image Retrieval Using Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The retrieval of images has become an essential task over the last two decades. Content-based image retrieval (CBIR) is an open field of research, driven by the abundance of data available on the internet and the increasing demand for effective image retrieval techniques. Various feature-based approaches, including global and local methods, have been established in the past; however, many of them were either overly complicated or limited to specific use cases. This paper proposes an extended statistical feature set-based CBIR method employing a support vector machine (SVM) for simple image retrieval. The article explores four different machine learning classifiers: binary tree, SVM, Gaussian SVM, and kernel-based classifiers. Images are converted to 2D grayscale for feature calculation, making the technique color-independent. The performance of the suggested method is tested and assessed using a standard dataset of versatile color images. The method aims to classify the dataset based on statistical parameters such as absolute mean, maximum, entropy, deviation, and 2D correlation of query images. Initially, the algorithm calculates the features of 500 photos divided into five types. Then, test and training data are gathered. The ultimate goal of the paper is to assess the accuracy of production for different kernel classifiers.

articleTitle: Proposed CNN Model for the Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a common chronic joint disorder affecting the health and quality of life for millions worldwide, particularly the elderly. This condition is distinguished by the progressive deterioration of cartilage in the knee joint, resulting in pain, stiffness, and limitations in physical function. Traditionally, the diagnosis of knee OA is based on clinical evaluations, patient-reported symptoms, and radiographic imaging. X-ray imaging is the most common modality due to its accessibility and cost-effectiveness. However, manual interpretation of X-ray images is prone to inter-observer variability and necessitates specialised knowledge, which can result in inconsistencies and delays in diagnosis. Deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), has demonstrated tremendous potential in automating medical image analysis, resulting in a more objective and efficient diagnostic approach. The study proposes a CNN-based model for classifying knee osteoarthritis using X-ray images. The dataset used in this study includes 6000 images divided into three categories: healthy, moderate, and severe. The proposed model achieves an overall accuracy of 96%, improving diagnostic accuracy and consistency by utilising CNNs to recognise complex patterns and features in images. This study’s findings have the potential to revolutionise the clinical management of knee OA by providing a robust, non-invasive diagnostic tool that improves the precision and efficiency of OA detection, thereby improving patient outcomes and lowering healthcare costs.

articleTitle: Environmental Pollution’s Effect on Biological Populations and Incomplete R-Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: An incomplete R-function mathematical model is used in the study to evaluate the impact of environmental contamination on biological populations. The findings reported here are typical of mathematical sciences, demonstrating several scenarios of interest under relevant parameter settings.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Driven Diagnosis A CNN-SVM Hybrid Approach for Automated Detection of Strawberry Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This hybrid approach is the combination of a Convolutional Neural Network and Support Vector Machine used in the automatic detection and classification of diseases in strawberry leaves. The architecture used, comprising three convolutional layers, three max-pampling layers, and one fully connected layer with ReLU for feature extraction, identifies the discriminative features from strawberry leaf images extracted using CNN and then feeds them into the SVM classifier for disease classification. The technique of transfer learning is followed in order to achieve the best model performance based on limited data. The efficiency of the model is measured based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The encouraging results given by the hybrid model CNN-SVM provide an effective framework for the automatic diagnosis of a lot of the diseases of the strawberry leaf, thus helping in the contribution to the best practices of managing crops and optimizing yields in strawberry cultivation.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-Cost Computer Vision System for Quantifying Ketone and Glucose in Urine Dipstick Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: <copy 979-8-3503-8459-8/24/$31.00 ©2024 IEEEUrinalysis is a crucial diagnostic tool, but current dipstick tests face limitations in accuracy and objectivity. While automated urine test strip readers could address these issues, existing devices are often expensive and inaccessible in resource-limited settings. This study presents the development of a low-cost, machine vision-based device for accurate quantification of ketone and glucose levels from colorimetric urine test strips. Our system employs computer vision algorithms to extract RGB color values from test strip images and maps them to analyte concentrations using calibration curves. The device consists of a Raspberry Pi module, a low-cost webcam, and a custom 3D-printed enclosure with controlled LED illumination, all integrated into a portable unit costing under Rs 10,000. We analyzed 8 urine samples with varying ketone and glucose concentrations, capturing images at 2-minute intervals from 2 to 10 minutes post-dipping. The system achieved 88.7% accuracy compared to gold-standard lab measurements, outperforming visual interpretation. This affordable and portable device has the potential to significantly improve access to reliable urinalysis in resource-limited settings, enabling early detection and better management of conditions like diabetes and kidney disease. By providing objective, quantitative results, it could enhance diagnostic accuracy and facilitate more timely interventions, ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes in underserved communities. This innovative solution addresses a significant barrier in healthcare diagnostics and represents a meaningful advance in point-of-care diagnostics, particularly for low-resource areas.

articleTitle: Automated Plant Disease Detection and Prevention Using Raspberry Pi and CNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper presents a framework leveraging Raspberry Pi for the detection and prevention of plant diseases, employing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithm for image analysis. With a focus on application in large-scale agricultural settings, the framework autonomously identifies signs of disease as they manifest on plant leaves. In agricultural research, timely detection of leaf diseases holds paramount importance, facilitating proactive monitoring of crops in the field through automated symptom recognition via CNN-based image processing. The term "disease" herein refers to various forms of plant damage. The primary objective of this paper is to employ this strategy for plant infection recognition through image processing, enabling timely alerts via email, SMS, and on-screen display of disease names to system owners. The automated symptom detection holds promise for enhancing agricultural yields, significantly reducing the reliance on chemical applications such as pesticides. By streamlining these technologies for complete automation, substantial cost savings can be realized, ultimately leading to increased farm productivity.

articleTitle: Developing a Novel Control System for a Two-wheeled Self-balancing Robot using a Dead-weight Pendulum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Existing two-wheeled self-balancing robots with the PID System and the inverted pendulum design exhibit certain disadvantages related to flexibility of use. This research aims to challenge and abate these issues using an innovative new control system that revolves around the seamless integration of a mechanism that allows the payload to act as a controlled dynamic pendulum inside the body of the robot. The configuration of the proposed control system gives the PID-based two-wheeled self-balancing robot an extra hand in its balancing and adaptive capabilities. In our prototype, the pendulum cum payload is attached to a servo motor whose motion is controlled to change the weight distribution of the body of the robot. During this research study, we have also created a mathematical equation that allows us to judge the combined effects of both the electronic PID and the dynamic pendulum mechanisms. And, our final experimental results show that not only does this mechanism improve the balancing capabilities of the robot with a huge range of payload masses, but also results in faster initial calibration and stabilization. In our conducted experiments, the prototype attained peak balancing performance with a payload of 55 grams, and we were also able to establish a positive relationship between the time taken to calibrate the robot body and the payload mass.

articleTitle: Insights and Performance Evaluation of Stable Diffusion Models with OpenVINO on Intel Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The use of deep learning to create images from text has emerged as an exciting and transformative field that blends natural language processing with computer vision. Throughout this review paper, the evolution of methods in the area of text-to-image synthesis is systematically explored to gain insights into art generation methods that do not require extensive hardware. This paper explores the integration of Stable Diffusion with the OpenVINO toolkit, a suite of performance-optimized tools designed to facilitate the deployment of AI models on various Intel hardware platforms. This paper provides insights into Stable Diffusion with OpenVINO and states the results of the model on Intel i5 hardware. A comparison of various text-to-image models has also been mentioned in this paper. Art generation models are developed to facilitate learners’ easy visualization of abstract topics, and analyzing the performance of the model on local hardware is one of our main objectives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Early Detection of Cardiovascular Disease through Feature Optimization Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: cardiovascular diseases are the most common reason for mortality around the world. Early detection of the ailment can help to reduce the mortality rate considerably. The ever-growing technologies like machine learning algorithms and deep learning models can be used for this purpose. The AI models thus developed can be used for health sector for assisting doctors in assessing the stage of the disease and detection and tracking of the clots in the cardio blood vessels. The proposed work uses two benchmark datasets for analysing the performance of various machine learning algorithms including KNN, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree and Random Forest. The performance was compares based on the AUC %. The method feature reduction were used here to reduce the computational complexity of the model. The results show that Random Forest Algorithm gave the best result when compared to other algorithms in case of UCI dataset and MLP classifier gave best results for Kaggle dataset.

articleTitle: Big Data Analysis and Applications in International Trade: Decision Optimization Based on Intelligent Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In the field of international trade, due to its wide range and complex interest relations, it is necessary to synthesize various information for analysis and decision-making. However, traditional data processing methods have been unable to meet the needs of enterprise development. As a new, efficient, safe and reliable solution, large database technology has been widely used in various fields and achieved good results. The purpose of this paper is to discuss and study the cross-department collaboration problem driven by intelligent algorithm through application examples. This paper first introduces the basic concepts, characteristics and relevant theoretical basis of inter-departmental collaboration. By studying the application of intelligent algorithms in interdepartmental collaboration, effective decision support tools are provided to deal with the complex situations in international trade. After that, this paper conducts a simulation test on the intelligent algorithm-driven decision optimization model, and the test results show that the test range of this model for the risk-return rate in trade is 0.04-0.09.

articleTitle: Computer Network Security Technology Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) technology continues to develop, cybersecurity issues are becoming increasingly prominent. Improving computer network security can further enhance the security of computer network information and avoid being affected by external environments. Applying AI technology to computer network security work can enhance the security of computer network information data, prevent illegal elements from illegally stealing and deleting computer network information data, and play a positive role in computer network security work. This article implemented the application of AI technology in computer network security through network security design, intrusion detection technology, and network security management technology based on AI technology. 82575 pieces of data were collected as data samples. To more accurately evaluate the actual effectiveness of AI in intrusion detection technology, it has been proven that AI has a very good effect in the utilization of computer network security technology.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Model for Predicting Internet Addiction in Teenage and Young Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Internet addiction is becoming one of the critical issues among teenagers and young university students. This habit not only negatively impacts the student’s learning performance, but also affects the student’s physical and mental health. This paper is focusing on designing a Machine Learning (ML) model for accurately identifying internet addiction. The model incorporates data preprocessing and feature selection techniques for reducing the computational complexity. Next, five different ML algorithms have been implemented and compared to identify appropriate ML algorithms. The identified ML model has been trained using the behavioral features of the students for predicting internet addiction. The experiments have been carried out and the performance of the models has been measured. The results demonstrate that a random forest classifier provides 83% accurate detection for university students and 96% accurate results are provided by an SVM-based classifier for teenager internet addiction detection. Therefore, by using the entire observation of experiments it is found that the proposed model can successfully identify internet addiction in students by analyzing the student's behavioral features.

articleTitle: Svelte EEG Net: Cross-Session Motor Imagery Classification for BCI-Controlled Prosthetic Arms using Novel Compact CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Cross-session motor imagery classification remains a critical bottleneck in BCI research, hampering the development of natural and intuitive BCI-controlled prosthetics. This study investigates the potential of Novel Compact Convolutional Neural Network, a deep learning architecture optimized for EEG data, for cross-session classification of motor imagery tasks using the left and right hands using the BNCI2014_001 dataset 9 subjects. We implement a skorch pipeline with MOABB for efficient data loading and evaluation, utilizing early stopping and epoch scoring for optimal training. Initial results show promising cross-session accuracy of 49.3%, suggesting Novel Compact convolutional neural network's potential for this challenging domain. However, deeper analysis reveals factors influencing performance and current limitations, including subject-specific variations, electrode selection, and hyperparameter tuning. This study paves the way for further exploration of Novel Compact convolutional neural network's capabilities in BCI-controlled prosthetics, potentially expanding to encompass control of all arm types and incorporating sensory feedback for enhanced naturalness.

articleTitle: Analysis of Language Recognition System Based on Cloud Computing Web Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: With the rise and popularization of cloud computing, information processing for schools, educational institutions, and individuals can gradually shift to the cloud. Therefore, it is particularly important to study the key technologies of online teaching platforms under cloud computing. This article is based on cloud computing technology, modular and multi-level architecture, combined with the concept of architecture, and constructs a data-driven teaching system structure. Cloud computing technology is a new type of online teaching architecture that can maximize the use of network information system resources according to different business needs and scenarios, establish new environments and models for information sharing, collaboration, and interactive online learning. This article introduces a cloud computing based analysis platform for language recognition systems aimed at improving the effectiveness of English teaching. Practical application has proven that this system can effectively solve some problems in current English teaching and play a significant role in students' English learning (the correlation between the content of the English Practice System (EPS) based on the technology in this article and the needs of students is 97%, and the accuracy is 99%).

articleTitle: YOLO: Redefining Real-Time Object Detection Accuracy and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Image classification, also known as object detection, is an advanced form of computer vision in which a network can predict objects in an image and point them out as bounding boxes. Classifying and recognizing objects in an image is just one aspect of object detection because it also involves localizing these objects and attracting bounding boxes around them. Since object detection involves image and video analysis, it has been of critical interest to researchers over the past few years. The previous object recognition method relies on manually created features and traditional and trainable algorithms. By using the YOLO (You Only Look Once) process, this research aims to perform real-time object detection. Regarding speed and performance, the YOLO algorithm is much more efficient than the existing model. Unlike existing algorithms that do not scan the entire image in single forward propagation, YOLO uses a neural network to predict binding boxes for the whole image. In comparison with existing algorithms, YOLO performs faster.

articleTitle: Mining sequential patterns from protein sequences associated with aggregation diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Protein aggregation is a hallmark of several neurodegenerative diseases. Mining patterns of amino acids from protein sequences aid in identifying regions of interest that can be validated clinically. Only a few studies have demonstrated the feasibility of employing Frequent Itemset Mining (FIM) algorithms for this task. However, these algorithms are not only computationally expensive but do not provide due consideration to the ordering of amino acids within a protein sequence. Apart from this, the number of patterns obtained remains sensitive to the input minimum support threshold. To overcome these limitations, the current study focuses on mining sequential patterns using the Top-k Sequential pattern mining algorithm that not only preserves the amino acid sequence but is also independent of any user input threshold. Across various protein sequences, the obtained sequential patterns were compared for similarity with frequent patterns by retaining as well as removing repeating amino acids. On average, about 89.31% non-repeating and 68.08% repeating sequential patterns were similar to the frequent patterns. Furthermore, a Jaccard Index close to 0.58 and 0.48 signifies the proximity of the sequential patterns with the frequent ones despite the absence of user-defined thresholds.

articleTitle: TensorFlow vs Theano: Issues and Challenges for Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: ensorFlow and Theano were popular deep learning frameworks for building and training neural networks, including image classification and NLP models. TensorFlow's evolution from a static graph-based approach to incorporating Eager Execution is examined, shedding light on its impact on ease of use and dynamic operations. Deep learning frameworks play a pivotal role in shaping the landscape of machine learning research and applications. Natural Language Processing (NLP) has witnessed remarkable advancements in recent years, owing much of its progress to deep learning frameworks. This paper presents an in-depth comparative analysis of two influential deep learning frameworks, TensorFlow and Theano, with a specific focus on their issues and challenges in the domain of NLP. Through a comprehensive exploration, this study aims to provide NLP practitioners and researchers with insights to navigate the complexities of framework selection for their linguistic tasks. By distilling the nuances of TensorFlow and Theano in the context of NLP challenges, this research equips NLP practitioners with a well-rounded understanding of the trade-offs and considerations in framework selection. Findings contribute to the informed decision-making process for choosing the appropriate framework based on the specific requirements of NLP tasks.

articleTitle: Abnormal Event Detection using Convolutional LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The development of smart CCTV systems heavily relies on the integration of abnormal event detection, human behavior analysis, and object recognition capabilities. These systems are designed to efficiently identify and respond to abnormal occurrences, suspicious behaviors, and potential threats within their monitored environments. Leveraging advanced technologies such as Machine Vision and Machine Learning, smart CCTV systems can effectively detect and classify anomalies present in the video feed. Typically employing frame-by-frame processing, these systems traditionally rely on Supervised Learning for training purposes; however, due to the diverse nature of anomalies and the impracticality of pre-training for all potential scenarios, there’s a gradual shift towards utilizing Unsupervised Learning and Semi-Supervised Learning methods. This transition aims to reduce the manual workload required for anomaly detection, thus enabling operators to focus on critical tasks. Moreover, to optimize storage efficiency, smart CCTV systems store abnormal events in high-quality formats while archiving normal scenarios in lower-quality formats. Additionally, these systems can extend their functionality through the implementation of distributed abnormality classification systems, where only abnormal events are transmitted to dedicated classifiers, streamlining the process and enhancing overall system performance. In essence, smart CCTV systems represent a sophisticated approach to surveillance, combining advanced technologies and intelligent algorithms to enhance security measures and minimize human intervention in anomaly detection and response processes.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Network Traffic Classification and Anomaly Detection Technology Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Malicious attacks against the Internet are emerging in endlessly. The traditional network architecture makes it impossible for network managers to obtain a complete network view, resulting in difficulties in network security maintenance and management. We have conducted research on network traffic identification, classification, and anomaly detection for network security control, aiming to further improve the efficiency of identification and detection, and enhance the network's security protection capabilities. A method based on the fusion of DPI and machine learning is proposed to achieve network traffic recognition and classification. On the basis of meeting accuracy requirements, DPI technology is used to effectively filter out useful information from network traffic, avoiding processing the entire data-set and reducing the cost of computing resources. Tests have shown that this method can effectively reduce computational resource overhead while ensuring the accuracy and real-time performance of classification.

articleTitle: An ensemble deep learning model based high precision automated analog meter reading utilizing EfficientDet detection and U-Net segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Analog meters are extensively utilized in contemporary sectors, including HVAC systems, pharmaceutical labs, manufacturing plants, and water treatment facilities. The present study proposes an enhanced approach that utilizes an ensemble framework to address reading mistakes and imprecise measurements caused by unequal or varying illumination in real-world scenarios. The proposed algorithm combines detection and segmentation methods to obtain precise measurements. The study uses advanced computer vision techniques to enhance the precision and effectiveness of automated analogue meter reading. The proposed method employs EfficientDet detection and U-Net segmentation to tackle issues related to the segmentation of pointer regions and interference caused by shadows. The algorithm’s effectiveness is shown by practical studies, demonstrating its robustness and flexibility in real-world scenarios. The optimum inference is achieved by the utilization of OpenVINO, enabling the simultaneous real-time monitoring of several meters, akin to its application in large-scale industrial environments.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Predictive Analytics for Epidemic Outbreaks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The goal of this project is to create a cloud-based predictive analytics system that tracks and forecasts COVID-19 outbreaks by utilizing Amazon Web Services (AWS). Using machine learning techniques and real-time data, the system aims to detect hotspots, improve resource allocation, and predict infection rates. Important objectives include integrating data, training the model, and deploying on AWS infrastructure. Involving health authorities facilitates proactive decision-making to enhance public health outcomes, lower transmission risks, and fortify epidemic response strategies. This study advances predictive analytics in epidemic control by utilizing cloud computing to deliver scalable and efficient solutions.

articleTitle: Cardiac Disease Prediction: A Deep Learning Approach using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: A complex organ, the heart is vital to human physiology. It has four chambers: left and right atria, left and right ventricles. These chambers are connected by valves and supported by several blood vessels. Cardiovascular disease diagnosis and treatment require understanding its anatomy. However, cardiovascular disease detection remains difficult. Modern healthcare makes cardiovascular disease diagnosis and detection harder, requiring precise and timely evaluations to determine effective treatment and avoid negative outcomes. Deep learning, a subset of artificial intelligence, has become a powerful tool for analyzing medical data and drawing conclusions. Deep learning cardiac illness diagnosis and detection advances. Clinical images, electrocardiograms (ECGs), patient records, and genetic data are processed using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTMs), and Deep Belief Networks. These methods allow deep learning algorithms to recognize complex patterns and risk indicators that imply cardiovascular diseases, enabling timely detection and targeted therapy. In addition, interpretability and explainability techniques have enabled the use of deep learning models in clinical contexts, giving healthcare practitioners vital decision-making tools. Deep learning can improve heart disease diagnosis and detection, improving patient outcomes and healthcare delivery, as this article shows.

articleTitle: Using XGBoost for Risk Stratification in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer Recurrence Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In this study, we developed machine learning models to predict the recurrence in patients with well-differentiated thyroid cancer, using XGBoost. Although the death rate from thyroid cancer is usually low, patients are often concerned about the chance of recurrence. Accurately assessing the risk of recurrence for each patient is crucial for determining appropriate medical management and follow-up protocols. We used a dataset of 383 patients who were monitored for at least 10 years within a 15-year timeframe. Despite the prevalence of thyroid malignancies, recurrent thyroid cancer remains poorly understood. Our study outcomes, utilizing the XGBoost machine learning model, demonstrated an accuracy of 98.48%.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Air Quality Index: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This study is about predicting AQI using different ML algorithms. Nowadays, AQI is declining, and to evaluate this there is a need for an effective AQI prediction model. This study uses two different learning algorithms, one is k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and another one is Random Forest. Both models have been used on the same dataset. Collected dataset and selected Features includes NH3, NO, NO2, NOx, PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, O3, benzene, toluene and xylene. To make the dataset concordant for the models, preprocess the data and handle missing values, and then divide it into training and testing. Train and test the models and evaluate the performance using different performance matrices. For KNN the accuracy is 80% and for Random Forest the accuracy is 83%. This shows that Random Forest is slightly more accurate than KNN.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wind Turbine Lifespan using Novel Vibration Sensor Data Techniques for Prognosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: An original method for wind turbine high-speed bearing condition prediction is given in this paper. The method uses unprocessed vibration-measuring sensor data. Bearings are divided into two groups using a 1D-CNN: Medium-life Expectancy (more than 15 days) and Short-life Expectancy (less than 15 days) following the computation of a Kurtosis Spectrogram for each of the 50 samples. The paper highlights the significance of early identification in predicting the Remaining-Useful Life (RUL) of machine components in order to maximise maintenance decisions and avoid breakdowns. Recall-based, a remarkable 90% accuracy is achieved by the 1D-CNN with Keras implementation. This work emphasises how this method may be used in alert systems to assist technical choices about component maintenance and guarantee the dependability and effectiveness of wind turbine systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization Based on AlphaZero Method Applied to Connection Games
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Open-ended learning, introduced by the DeepMind team in 2021, represents a novel AI approach to achieve multi-objective optimization, allowing it to simultaneously handle multiple tasks, whereas traditional AI is optimized only for a single task. This study describes an AI implementation similar to open-ended learning using relatively familiar technologies and game rules, making it adaptable to two different game rule sets. Experimental results indicate that, given equal training time, multi-objective AlphaZero outperforms the single-objective optimized version of AlphaZero. Training using both rule sets impacts the neural network. Our results indicate that simpler training data can accelerate the model’s initial learning phase without compromising performance across the two rule sets. Multi-objective training is found to enhance the overall efficiency and effectiveness of neural network learning. Specifically, incorporating simpler rule sets accelerates early-stage training and helps lay the foundation for learning more complex rules. The findings suggest that leveraging the interaction between different levels of rule complexity can achieve more balanced and comprehensive training outcomes, ultimately resulting in a more generalizable AI model.

articleTitle: Small, but Mighty: Lightweight ML-Enabled Intrusion Detection Framework for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) have become an integral component of contemporary vehicular technology. This technology provides advanced features like traffic and weather reports and collision prevention to create a sophisticated driving experience. Unfortunately, this infrastructure can become victim to cyber-attacks like intrusions that aim to compromise VANET operations. In this paper, we propose a novel lightweight machine learning (ML)-based intrusion detection framework for VANETs. The algorithm developed utilizes dimensionality reduction to reduce the operational footprint of our training data so that it is easier to train and deploy ML-enabled intrusion detectors for protecting VANET infrastructures. Results showcase that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K=3$</tex> provides us with high performance and low operational requirements. Through this, we achieve efficient performance for protecting VANETs against intrusions while decreasing the overall operational footprint of the framework.

articleTitle: Scalable Big Data Analysis and Processing Technology for Intelligent Traffic Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The improvement of people's living standards, every family has a private car, and large trucks used in industry are the reason for the continuous increase in the traffic flow, and traffic congestion has become an increasingly serious problem. When traffic congestion becomes an urgent problem that restricts the development of the city, intelligent traffic control becomes a technology that can improve traffic efficiency and traffic safety. When we look at the traffic system from the perspective of big data, we will find that the data involved in the intelligent transportation system is very large, and the traditional method of data analysis and processing is no longer applicable. This research conducts in-depth research on the various data sources involved in the intelligent transportation system, and analyzes the features and scale of these data sources. A distributed computing based scalable big data analysis framework is proposed in order to solve the problem of big data analysis and processing. The framework employs parallel computing and distributed storage technology to process large-scale data efficiently, and to obtain real-time analysis results. The scalability of the proposed scalable big data analysis framework and the data preprocessing methods was verified by experimental evaluation, and the performance was highlighted. The research results show that the big data analysis technology can process and analyze big data generated in ITS, and provide important decision support for intelligent transportation control based on the true results of the analysis.

articleTitle: Navigating the Challenge of Small Data: Optimizing Utility Company Net Revenue Forecasting with Robust Modeling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Forecasting net revenue with limited data presents significant challenges, particularly in utility sectors where economic forecasting accuracy is crucial for strategic planning. This paper explores the efficacy of various predictive models on a small dataset of 105 data points from a utility company, aiming to forecast net revenue for the year 2024 based on net booking counts. We compared traditional regression, tree-based, and time series forecasting models, specifically focusing on Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and SARIMAX, to address the typical issues of overfitting and multicollinearity encountered in small datasets. Our methodology included feature engineering to enhance model input, such as lagged variables and rolling means, to capture temporal dependencies and seasonality better. The results indicate a general tendency of regression and tree-based models to overfit given the small data size, whereas the SARIMAX model, using net booking count as an exogenous variable, provided more reliable forecasts with an R-squared value of 62%. This study not only underscores the limitations of conventional models in handling small datasets but also highlights the relative robustness of SARIMAX in capturing underlying data patterns crucial for effective forecast modeling in utility management.

articleTitle: Securing Asymmetric Key Cryptography in 6G Wireless and Mobile Environments: A Comprehensive Review and Proposed Hybrid Cryptosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The introduction of 6G networks and the ongoing advancement in wireless and mobile technologies pose several security issues which need to be addressed for privacy-sensitive information or conversations. The assurance of Data confidentiality, integrity and authenticity is majorly based on Public Key Cryptography (PKC) especially in case when Digital signatures, key distribution and secure communication channel are required. The PKC security, however, is limited due to the dynamism of wireless and mobile contexts as well as constrained device resources that are facing constantly changing attack vectors. This study examines the existing practices (for asymmetric key management, distribution and creation) in these scenarios to find out potential vulnerabilities that are exploitable by attackers. To address these difficulties, the review proposes an original crossover cryptosystem that joins different cryptographic methods, including lattice-based encryption, quantum-resistant algorithms, and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), to upgrade protection from different dangers. The discoveries and commitments of this examination have critical ramifications for the improvement of secure and solid cryptographic conventions in 6G organizations, defending confidential data and correspondences in remote and versatile conditions.

articleTitle: Biometric Authentication Systems in Banking: A Technical Evaluation of Security Measures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Biometric authentication structures have come to be increasingly popular in recent years as a way of protecting touchy information and transactions within the banking area. Those structures use specific bodily or behavioral characteristics, which includes fingerprints, iris scans, facial recognition, voice reputation, or typing patterns, to confirm someone’s identification. In this technical evaluation, we are able to talk about the numerous security features employed through biometric authentication structures in banking, their effectiveness, and capability vulnerabilities. One of the key safety features in biometric authentication systems is the enrollment procedure. For the duration of enrollment, a user’s biometric characteristics are gathered and saved in a database. This record is later used for verification purposes. To ensure safety, proper encryption strategies should be used to guard the biometric records. Encryption algorithms such as advanced Encryption widespread (AES) can guard the records in transit and at relaxation. Another vital security degree is the usage of livens detection. This is a method used to prevent spoofing attacks, in which an attacker attempts to fool the gadget by way of the usage of a fake biometric pattern. Livens detection methods use various parameters, inclusive of movement, skin texture, and thermal detection, to differentiate between real and faux samples.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement Using Gaussian Pyramid, Laplacian Pyramid and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Underwater imaging is essential for capturing submerged environments and it faces significant challenges due to light attenuation, water turbidity and color distortion. This paper presents a novel technique to enlighten underwater image quality through a combination of multiscale image processing techniques like Gaussian and Laplacian pyramids, combined with Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to enhance underwater image. In this paper, five different datasets namely, UIEB, EUVP, RUIE, USR and U45 datasets are used to representing various underwater environments and conditions. Four filtering techniques are employed to sharpen images and the resulting enhancements are showcased. From the result, it is found that the parameters including PSNR, UISM, UICM, PCQI and UIQM reach their maximum value for Laplacian of Gaussian method. Conversely, the gamma correction technique exhibits better performance, particularly in terms of UCIQE and CCQ metrics. It is clear from the suggested method that is applied to the UIEB Real World Underwater Datasets various parameter values are evaluated. The PCQI value is 0.0119, the UIQM value is 0.9998, and the UCIQE value is 30.455, according to the results. It shown in comparison to the other approaches that have been proposed earlier, the UCIQE value is improvised. The proposed method offers a superior solution for enhancing underwater images.

Author Keywords: Laplacian pyramid and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization

articleTitle: CommandSense: Actions-Objects-Results Prediction from Natural Language Commands using Fine-Tuned GPT-3.5 Turbo
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This research delves into the use of OpenAI's GPT-3.5 Turbo model to transform human commands provided to a virtual agent in a virtual simulated environment into action, object and results. For this, the sophisticated ALFRED dataset in text format was reformatted into JSONL format. Central to our evaluation methodology were the BLEU scores (BLEU-1, BLEU-2, BLEU-3, and BLEU-4) and Edit Distance. The fine-tuning of the GPT-3.5 Turbo model achieved impressive results, with BLEU-1 reaching 84%, BLEU-2 at 50%, BLEU-3 at 42%, and BLEU-4 at 32%, indicating a high degree of linguistic correspondence in simpler constructs and reasonable competence in more complex structures. The overall Edit Distance recorded was 2.67, reflecting the model's accuracy in translating commands into actions. This study contributes critical insights into the capabilities of advanced AI in interpreting complex human commands, paving the way for broader applications in various real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Enhanced Kidney Segmentation: Evaluating U-Net and Attention U-Net with Cross-Entropy and Focal Loss Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The rising occurrence of chronic kidney disease represents a significant health concern, impacting over 10% of individuals. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) biomarkers identify pathological alterations, are non-invasive, and can help lessen biopsy requirements and complications in chronic kidney disease patients. Total volume is the most assessed metric in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease patients, assisting in tracking chronic kidney disease progression. Kidney segmentation is essential for evaluating renal volume. Nevertheless, it often relies on manual segmentation, which is time-consuming and highly subjective. However, Deep Learning (DL) techniques have led to creating algorithms that provide accurate, cost-effective, and user-independent outcomes. Therefore, this study explores DL-based strategies for kidney segmentation, particularly U-Net and Attention U-Net. Both architectures were assessed with the standard cross-entropy loss function and a focal cross-entropy loss function. Ultimately, the proposed methods were used for both 2-class and 3-class segmentation to improve the segmentation of border regions. The highest Dice coefficient achieved on the testing set was 0.966.

articleTitle: Physiological Conversations For Detection and Prediction of Emotion Recognition Using Scheduling Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: By anticipating behavioural patterns and preventing the spread of harmful memes, machine learning enhances psychology. Cutting-edge algorithms identify meme humour and assess its influence on communities. Psychology’s ability to forecast future behaviours and societal difficulties is enhanced by this combination. New tools are produced via interdisciplinary collaboration in computer science, data science, and psychology. This combination strengthens psychology’s capacity for accurate prediction and practical application. The combination of machine learning and psychology is expected to advance understanding of human behaviour. This synergy promotes interventions that improve mental health and the general well-being of society in addition to helping to fathom the intricacies of the mind.

articleTitle: Investigating the Advantages of AI-driven Predictive Analysis in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: AI-pushed predictive evaluation can revolutionize healthcare. With the usage of superior predictive models and machine algorithms, AI can discover styles and appropriately expect consequences for clinical treatments and remedies. It may assist clinicians in making more informed decisions and ensuring certain affected persons' safety. In this summary, we assess the benefits of imposing AI-driven predictive analysis in healthcare AI-driven predictive evaluation permits the usage of state-of-the-art fashions that can correctly predict medical outcomes. It allows doctors and healthcare carriers to limit risks and discover ability problems earlier than they grow to be intricate. By way of leveraging available information, such as scientific records, genomic information, and more, AI can accurately generate insights and guidelines for remedy and prognosis. Moreover, AI-pushed predictive evaluation is incredibly capable of figuring out destructive drug reactions and different interactions among drugs, in addition to providing perception into drug interactions among illnesses and other conditions. AI-driven predictive evaluation has numerous packages in healthcare and may be used to pick out capacity mistakes before they occur. AI can analyze a large variety of records and generate reports on the consequences. It will assist healthcare providers in making the proper decisions in relation to imparting top-quality care for sufferers. Moreover, AI can be used to expand customized treatment plans, which are custom-designed to every patient’s unique state of affairs. It may be extraordinary.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition using Improved Convolutional Neural Networks for Specially Abled
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper thoroughly studies the turn of events and assessment of a Hand Gesture Recognition model using a custom dataset of 565 pictures addressing 30 different gesture-based communication activities. The dataset, carefully organized to incorporate a comprehensive exhibit of hand motions, looks, and body developments, is a fundamental asset for preparing AI models to precisely perceive and group these activities. The proposed model, which utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image handling, exhibits an exceptional exactness in recognizing and grouping hand signals. This elevated degree of exactness not only approves the model's capacity to decipher gesture-based communication but also highlights the capability of such advances in upgrading correspondence availability for people with hearing impedances. The paper features the meaning of the dataset's exhaustive portrayal of communication through signing activities, accentuating the significance of envisioning and understanding the intricacies of gesture-based communication to foster precise and powerful correspondence technologies. The study's discoveries add to the gesture-based communication acknowledgment field and move further innovative work in making more available and compelling correspondence advances for people with hearing debilitations.

articleTitle: Optimizing Metal Casting Quality: Harnessing CNN-SVM Synergies for Enhanced Fault Recognition and Productivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The main points of this study's findings in creating a prediction model to detect gas faults in metal casting processes are summarized in the abstract. Four different defect classes—Open hole, Blow hole, Pinhole, and Shrinkage—are the subject of this study. This model shows excellent performance metrics in all of these classes. Precision demonstrates the model's capacity to reduce false positives; it measures the percentage of correctly detected occurrences across all instances that belong to a specific fault class. Precision varies from 90.91% to 94.29%. Recall, that another metric that shows how well the model captures instances of each defect type, ranges from 91.80% to 94.59%. Recall is defined as the percentage of correctly detected occurrences of an error class among every instance of that class. The harmonic range of precision and recall, or F1-score, emphasizes the durability of the prediction system, with 91.74% to 93.96% as ranges. The support values also show how many examples for each problem class there are in the dataset, which sheds light on the distribution and frequency of various defect kinds. Notably, our model achieves an extraordinarily high 97% accuracy across all fault types. Furthermore, the precision, recall, and F1-score macro, weighed, and micro averages consistently produce strong values of 93.0% and 93.1%, respectively. These results confirm the validity and effectiveness of our prediction model, which has implications for improving metal casting process defect recognition and classification accuracy, leading to increased industrial productivity and quality.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality-based Sudoku Solver with Training Module to Improve Cognitive Skills
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper presents an interactive Augmented Reality (AR) Sudoku Scanner application that leverages Computer Vision and a dancing link algorithm to solve Sudoku puzzles in real-time. The application employs various techniques, including thresholding, greyscaling, and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model, to accurately recognize Sudoku grids and individual digits. Beyond the scanner, the proposed app integrates a playable Sudoku game with multiple difficulty levels, hint functionality, and sign-up/login-based user authentication for a personalized experience. A user leaderboard further incentivizes engagement. Furthermore, a feedback mechanism is implemented to gather user data and perform basic data analysis. This analysis, visualized through charts and diagrams, enables us to understand user interactions and optimize the application’s user interface and experience. It was observed that the proposed app helped to improve cognitive skills in younger users compared to older ones.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Driven Decision making in Business Analytics for Financial Sector using Ensemble Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In today's rapidly evolving financial landscape, banks stand in critical conditions to capitalize on advanced technologies to enhance their competitiveness. By harnessing AI/ML models, finance sectors like banks can optimize customer interactions, streamline operations, and drive down expenses while delivering unparalleled user experiences. These powerful tools enable banks to excel in three critical domains: real-time customer engagement, automated workflows, and data-driven decision-making. Deploying AI/ML solutions at scale offers a distinct advantage over competitors, fostering substantial gains for clients, stakeholders, and the institution alike. Credit card risk assessment, insurance claim prediction, and targeted marketing initiatives are just some examples where AI can deliver exceptional results. Algorithms like K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Logistic Regression, in this paper prove effective in classifying decision-making problems within the finance sector with great recall, precision and F1 Score above 0.8 in majority cases. We have well utilized stacking classifier ensemble technique for better results.. A comprehensive approach to AI integration encompasses all aspects of the business, including product development, risk management, compliance, and customer service. By embracing this transformational technology, banks can achieve sustainable growth, foster innovation, and maintain a strong foothold in the ever-changing world of finance. As AI continues to revolutionize the banking industry, forward-thinking organizations will reap the rewards of early adoption, setting new standards for excellence and efficiency. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Different Optimization Technique for Ant Cluster Head and Routing Protocol in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is a revolutionary meta-heuristic area dedicated to intelligent issue exploration and optimization. The communal foraging activities of humpback whales inspired this evolutionary optimization strategy. WOA is a population-based search optimization algorithm that mimics the intricate foraging behaviors of humpback whales to give an intelligent approach to looking for the best solutions. This approach has been used to solve a variety of real-world issues, such as numerical optimization, feature selection, and clustering. However, the proposed model routes through CH, with the choice of CH made using the ALWO algorithm based on constraints, namely energy and delay. The suggested E- ALWO method computes the optimal and secure path for the data transfer process based on the fitness measure. WOA provides more exploration capability and is not constrained by the local search of previous approaches, staying indifferent to the initial solution selection. The method outperformed the most common optimization algorithms

articleTitle: Enhancing Heart Murmur Detection: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Models Utilizing Digital Stethoscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Machine learning has proven to be a powerful tool across many domains including healthcare. Heart sound classification using machine learning can revolutionize cardiac care by improving diagnostic accuracy, enabling early intervention, and facilitating personalized treatment strategies. However, obtaining labeled data for classification model training can be difficult, especially for rare or complex conditions. Furthermore, classifying heart sounds accurately can be challenging due to the variability in sound patterns and the presence of noise which requires preprocessing. In this paper, two machine learning models were trained and evaluated using DenseNet architecture on the CirCor DigiScope Phonocardiagram dataset and an ensemble of Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Decision Tree (DT) algorithms on a custom dataset curated by our partner, Tech4Life. The F1 score of the CirCor trained model was 75%. This is our effort to advance the application of machine learning in heart sound classification.

articleTitle: Is the VGG-19 Road Segmentation Method better than the Customized UNET Method?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The main reason for coming up with self-driving cars is to enhance the safety of cars on the road by improving and reducing the occurrence of traffic accidents. Self-driving cars rely on advanced systems known as Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADASs) that help in perceiving the driving environment despite being on the road. Automobile lane detection is repeatedly considered effective in building up the recognition of the nearest lanes. Is it capable of discerning lane markings and objects on the side of the road or, topologically, it does not have to make a rolling contact? To answer this query, hence we apply road segmentation techniques that involve delineation of objects of interest along the road. In this paper, we compared two models named VGG-19 and UNET by observing their accuracy in detecting road lanes, objects, and cars. We find that the VGG-19 model achieves superior accuracy, about 40% accuracy with 93% precision in detecting complex road structures compared to the UNET model in our 95 images. This research contributes to finding a novel technique for semantic segmentation in the context of autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Enhanced Security Measures for Government and Military: ANN and Decision Tree Approach to Counter VPN Malicious Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: For governments, armed forces and related institutions, which need to be highly secure places ensuring all possible attacks on national security, are repelled. This includes the use of state-of-the-art cyber-security techniques. Strict encryption protocols must be observed for secure communication channels must be guaranteed at all times. A watchful eye is also of paramount importance. Governments and military structures can shrink the risks by emphasizing security of government actions and promoting an offensive defense. As the importance of government and military affairs grows, the research paper on an advanced secure framework to enforce security on Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). Based on a method using both Artificial Neural Networks, decision tree algorithms and fusion strategies, this legislation will improve the ability to find solve uncertainty threats. Moreover, the implementation of an advanced chip can give advance notice malicious attacks. That in turn also means the authors will be able to take proactive measures against them. The integrated approach has undergone strict review and test. The accuracy rate is 85%. All of this demonstrates its effectiveness in keeping government and military networks safe. By acting to detect and block malicious transmissions on a VPN, our system ensures sensitive information in satellites, aircraft and other critical infrastructure can keep its confidentiality, integrity and availability. Through the provision of a framework for security, it must be admitted that advanced security truly is what has been happening all along. By combining ANN, Decision Tree algorithms and a sophisticated chip, this model can offer an all-round defense against even the most advanced cyber threats. It will ultimately improve the security nature of government and military operations.

articleTitle: Knee Osteoarthritis Prediction using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (OA) is a frequently encountered degenerative joint disease that has a major global health impact. An early and precise assessment of OA severity is vital for implementing swift measures and personalized treatment plans. This research aims to use complex machine learning algorithms, including CNN and Transfer Learning with class dropping, to accurately assess the severity of osteoarthritis (OA) in the knee using X-ray images. By utilizing CNN’s deep learning capabilities, we examine the network’s capacity to recognize complex patterns and features present in X-ray images linked to various phases of osteoarthritis. In addition, we investigate Transfer Learning, which makes use of trained models like ResNet to extract insights from massive datasets in unrelated fields. Two-class classification achieved the highest accuracy among class dropping studies, with 98.26% using a custom dense layer, 97% using random forest, and 92% using SVM. The findings provide interesting pathways for rapid and personalized therapies in addressing this common degenerative joint disease, utilizing machine learning approaches.

articleTitle: A Fusion Approach of Edge-Cloud Computing for Optimizing Power Usage in Surveillance via Advanced Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced surveillance system aimed at tackling prevalent issues like limited data storage space, delays in event detection, accurate situation prediction, and high power consumption. To address these challenges, the paper proposes the use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) technology, leveraging its capabilities to enhance system efficiency. The architectural framework outlined in the study primarily focuses on optimizing energy utilization and video processing by efficiently leveraging both edge and cloud computing resources. The first and most important feature of this study is a thorough investigation of energy consumption levels specific to the specified area. Valuable insights are drawn from interactions with the systems, which play an important role in developing machine learning models capable of detecting optimal lines of activity based on acquired information about the patterns. In addition, our research focuses heavily on evaluating how well proposed solutions reduce latency, improve event accuracy, and minimize power consumption costs. It was analyzed and tested in detail to ensure that the system, suggested for the resolution of problems, meets and exceeds performance standards. This all-inclusive model introduces the study as a full-fledged probe into state-of-the-art technological advancements aimed at boosting surveillance efficiency.

articleTitle: Enhancing Speech Emotion Recognition Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The research highlights the significance of speech processing in various applications, particularly emotion recognition, and its importance in understanding human behavior and mental health. Despite the challenges in accurately predicting emotions from speech, recent research has achieved accuracy rates of 80-90% using techniques such as Bayesian Networks, Neural Networks, and Deep Neural Networks. However, issues like semantic independence, noise, and data volume still pose challenges. The study proposes the use of deep neural networks to analyze speech emotions, leveraging the mix database and techniques like noise cancellation and feature extraction to improve accuracy.

articleTitle: A Fine-Tuned Transformer Model for Dysarthric Speech with Spectrograms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This study examines the enhancement of communication for individuals with dysarthria speech disorder that impairs control of speech muscles through Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) technologies. While transformer and neural attention-based sequence-to-sequence models have achieved state-of-the-art results in typical speech-to-text applications, their adaptation for dysarthric speech recognition presents significant challenges. These include the unique articulatory variation and a lack of substantial training data characteristic of dysarthric speech. To bridge this gap, our research introduces a novel Dysarthric Speech Transformer, which incorporates a deep transformer architecture specifically designed to accommodate the complexities of dysarthric speech patterns. To overcome the hurdle of data scarcity, we employ a two-phase transfer learning strategy that leverage high-quality clear speech data, alongside innovative neural freezing configurations, to enhance model training and effectiveness. Our methodology is validated through rigorous training on the UASpeech(M12) and TORGO datasets, which are tailored for speaker-specific dysarthric ASR. The results indicate a substantial improvement in recognition accuracy, underscoring the efficacy of our specialized transformer model. Further, our study explores the synergistic potential of combining signal processing techniques with deep learning, suggesting that this approach could lead to breakthroughs in ASR system performance for individuals with severe dysarthria. This integration promises not only to refine the accuracy of dysarthric speech recognition, but also to extend the accessibility and usability of ASR technologies for those most in need.

articleTitle: Deploying Healthcare Monitoring System For Elderly Patient Care using IoT and Neural Network Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Utilizing Internet of Things (IoT) technology in the healthcare sector can revolutionize the care provided to individuals. This study illustrates the application of IoT in ensuring continuous healthcare for elderly patients, particularly focusing on scenarios like epidemiology in rehabilitation centers, intensive care units (ICU), and home health care. The research integrates a variety of sensors, machine learning algorithms, and cloud computing to establish a healthcare system driven by IoT. With a participant pool of 50 individuals, including both healthy adults and those with various ailments, the study employs Short-Term Memory (LSTM), decision trees, and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models to analyze sensor data, specifically temperature and heart rate measurements. The primary objective is to identify uncertainties and facilitate timely interventions. Results indicate that ANN surpasses LSTM and tree models in parameter estimation, displaying superior accuracy and F1 scores in anomaly detection while minimizing false negatives. This use of predictive ability has the chance of reforming treatment through early detection and administration of treatments. This research, in short, exemplifies the importance of integrating prognostic analytics in health systems that support IoT; in other words, it enables continuous monitoring, forecasting, and access to care requirements concerning changing forms of illness. From a scientific perspective, this work is seen as being proactive because it adopts green medical materials and uses IoT-based methods so that control performance may be improved for the patients.

articleTitle: Advancements in Crowd Analysis: Datasets and Deep Learning Approaches for Enhanced Surveillance and Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The study explores crowd control in densely populated metropolitan settings, emphasizing the necessity of striking a compromise between convenience and security. It looks at communication strategies, crowd management techniques, and emergency readiness. It also looks at the function of smart surveillance systems, which study crowd data and behaviors, particularly for anomaly detection. The study addresses the difficulties associated with crowd estimation in populated areas and suggests deep learning methods to improve precision. It makes a distinction between crowd management and control, emphasizing the part data analytics plays in urban dynamics. There is a discussion of how urbanization affects crowd gatherings and a plea for effective crowd control to avoid chaos. The project integrates technology with health management for huge events, advancing automated surveillance and crowd control. It emphasizes how feature alignment and semi-supervised learning can be used to handle domain adaptability in crowd counting. In this research survey, we explore real-time object detection using the YOU ONLY LOOK ONCE (YOLO) algorithm and convolutional neural networks (CNNs).The goal of the study is to create safer and more ordered urban areas by making a significant contribution to computer vision and crowd control.

articleTitle: Fostering Viability of Flipped- Techno Approach on English Language Learning: Simple Moderation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The purpose of the study is to explore the role of interactive and collaborative activities with techno- aids in improving and grasping English as Second language. The paper is targeted to study student’s perception on interactive pedagogy and flipped techno-learning as the best tool to promote Communicative English Language skills. The aim is to address the gap in higher education, which often focuses on theoretical concepts instead of practical, spontaneous interactions. The results of the research are computed by a statistical approach which suggests that face to face interaction, social networking and technology assists in the development of language and interpersonal skills of the students. The instrument used for study is a Questionnaire where Two Hundred and Fifteen students point their perception towards teaching and learning English language. The present study is an empirical study, to investigate the effectiveness of technology on ELL. The paper also investigates the impact of motivation perspective as a moderating variable.
