It has been reflected through the results that both Motivational Perspective and Technology have a significant relation with ELL individually, however, it is also observed that motivation perspective does not play a moderating role in reinforcing the positive relationship between Technology and ELL.

articleTitle: PUF-Based Authentication System with Resilience against Multi-Faceted Attacks for Blockchain-based IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Now a days, blockchain based IOT networks are gaining popularity for the unlimited space and robust security mechanism. Blockchain is the best solution for the IoT devices to store the huge amount of data generated by them with utmost privacy and security using distributed ledger. However, the resource constrained IoT devices having low computing power are unable to meet the huge computing requirements of data mining in blockchain networks. This paper has proposed a robust Physically Unclonable Function (PUF)-based authentication system to replace the popular consensus algorithms by a lightweight hardware-based authentication mechanism without compromising the security and privacy. The proposed ring oscillator based PUF modules fortify users' credentials and withstand various types of attacks in decentralized and tamper-resistant blockchain based IOT network with significant reduction in latency and power consumption. Attack analysis is done to compare the vulnerabilities of both the proposed and conventional systems to prominent blockchain attacks. The results of attack analysis demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms the conventional PoW system.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Assessment of Deep Learning Models for Multi Disease Detection in Brain MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This study delves into the analysis of various CNN models for detecting Alzheimer's disease from MRI images. The Alzheimer's dataset comprises four classes representing very mild, mild, and moderate stages of Alzheimer's, as well as healthy conditions. Standard CNN models, including VGGNets, ResNets, and advanced models like MobileNet, are evaluated to determine the most effective approach for extracting features relevant to these stages of Alzheimer's. Among the 10 models assessed, MobileNet-V2 demonstrates the highest accuracy at 91%. The MBConvolution block within MobileNet-V2 proves particularly adept at extracting the pertinent features for this task. Consequently, this research facilitates the detection of Alzheimer's across various stages, thereby providing a foundation for researchers to develop new models with improved performance.

articleTitle: Deepfake Detection using InceptionResNetV2 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The ability to create a nearly similar human-generated image—also known as a "deep fake"—has become very easy due to the increasing processing capacity of deep learning algorithms. It is easy to imagine scenarios where these deepfakes with morphing faces are the driving force behind terrorist acts, political turmoil, revenge porn, and private blackmail. This article presents an innovative deep learning-based technique that can reliably identify authentic pictures from phoney ones created by artificial intelligence. The technique is capable of automatically differentiating between replacement deep fakes and reproductions and leverages transfer learning by incorporating the InceptionResNetV2 pre-trained on ImageNet, a large image database. To replicate real-time scenarios and enhance the model's performance on real-time data, the method is evaluated on a substantial amount of balanced dataset. It also shows how the system may achieve competitive outcomes by employing a rather simple and dependable technique.

articleTitle: Fortifying Oximeter Data Protection: Safeguarding with Frodokem and NTRU Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The present study suggests a novel way to combine NTRU and FrodoKEM encryption algorithms with blockchain technology to improve the security of oximeter data in healthcare settings. These post-quantum cryptography techniques defend against threats from quantum computing by addressing flaws in conventional encryption, while blockchain ensures the integrity and transparency of data. Real-time applications in resource-constrained healthcare settings are particularly suited for FrodoKEM due to its resistance to Shor’s algorithm and NTRU’s efficiency. The encryption procedure is optimized throughout implementation to guarantee the least possible influence on oximeter performance. Blockchain technology is integrated into the system to securely record access to patient health data, ensuring transparency and auditability. Each access request and data transaction is cryptographically signed and added to an immutable ledger, protecting the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive patient health information against changing cybersecurity threats. The study demonstrates that employing FrodoKEM and NTRU encryption algorithms in conjunction with blockchain successfully secures oximeter data, ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive patient health information against quantum computing threats in healthcare settings. This combined approach provides a robust solution to protect patient health data from unauthorized access and tampering, leveraging the strengths of both encryption and blockchain technologies.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Malware Detection in Android: A Practical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Today's society heavily depends on online communities, which host a wide variety of social networks and public and private services. These demands led to the creation of Android, the world's most popular mobile operating system. The wide range of features and capabilities offered by freely installable third-party apps is largely responsible for this success. While focusing on the positive aspects of technology use, it is vital to keep in mind the potential negative consequences like privacy breaches, data theft, and malware infections that could compromise personal information and device security, especially if negligence or overuse of technology is present. This article discusses a systematic review of ML-based Android malware detection techniques. It provides a critical analysis of a number of carefully selected articles, highlighting their methods and conclusions. To support this study, we also present our own analysis and findings, for which an evaluation of diverse ML models with 123,453 applications and 5,560 malware samples from the DREBIN dataset was done to classify apps as malicious and benign. Preprocessing was done on the dataset to address missing values and perform label encoding. To cope with the issue of class imbalance, we used SMOTE an efficient ML technique that handles imbalance issues efficiently. We have applied five different ML algorithms, The results show that among all the techniques, Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machines (SVM) with various kernels (linear, polynomial, RBF), Sequential Neural Network (NN), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), and Logistic Regression (LR), the sequential neural network model outperformed other methods with 99% accuracy. Additionally, the process identifies areas for future research and improvement in ML-based Android malware detection techniques.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Secure Image Transmission with Rubik’s, Chaos, DNA, and Homomorphic Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper presents a framework for secure image encryption with the comparison of qualitative and quantitative aspects of fewnovel and established encryption methods. Rubik’s Method, DNA Encoding, Chaotic Systems, and Homomorphic encryption are evaluated for their efficiency in image encryptions. An input image is subjected to successive shifting operations in order to encrypt it using Rubik’s method, with the sum of pixel values and predefined keys serving as the basis. The Chaos Map encryption is demonstrated with the use of Arnold Cat map to jumble pixel placements. Further intricacy is introduced by DNA encoding, which converts pixel values into DNA sequences. DNA method is also considered as a hyper-chaotic map. To depict Homomorphic encryption, the Paillier cryptosystem is to perform additive and multiplicative operations on the image. We can learn a lot about the efficiency of encryption from evaluation measures like histograms, Unified Average Changing Intensity, and Computational Costs.

articleTitle: Advancements in Noise Reduction Techniques in ECG Signals: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) and Electrocardiography play crucial roles in monitoring heart functionality and diagnosing heart diseases. However, the reliability of these methods can be compromised due to various sources of noise, including climatic conditions, patient-body contact, and power fluctuations. Among these noises that most affect the ECG signals are three i.e. Baseline Wander (BLW), Powerline Interface (PLI), and Motion Artifact (MA). Baseline Wander refers to low-frequency components while Powerline Interface is caused by interference from the power grid, typically at 50 or 60 Hz. Motion Artifact results from patient movement, leading to distortions in the ECG signal. This paper undertakes a comprehensive review on the different noises affecting the ECG signals and surveys various methodologies to effectively minimize noise interference. Recognizing the significance of addressing these challenges, the noise reduction techniques aim to enhance the accuracy and reliability of ECG signal analysis. By mitigating the impact of Baseline Wander, Powerline Interface, and Motion Artifact, the techniques or methods help to improve the diagnosis and patient care. Through the implementation of advanced signal processing and filtering methods, the goal is to ensure that healthcare professionals can rely on more accurate ECG data, thereby facilitating more precise diagnoses and treatment decisions. Ultimately, these efforts seek to elevate the overall quality of patient care in cardiovascular health.

articleTitle: Categorical Prediction and Design Implementation for Triple Marker Test Using Clustering Algorithms and Validations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: <copy 979-8-3503-8459-8/24/$31.00 ©2024 IEEEAn innovative method for anticipating possible birth abnormalities during pregnancy is described in this study. The triple marker test, a prenatal screening tool used by the system, analyzes the levels of the mother's blood components beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), estriol (E3), and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). In the past, this test required labeled data for analysis— positive or negative for birth abnormalities. However, our method makes use of unlabeled data and an unsupervised machine- learning technique called k-means clustering. The unlabeled data is initially classified into two clusters by the algorithm using k- means clustering, which most likely corresponds to pregnancies with a high and low risk of birth abnormalities. The data points are then given labels (positive or negative) based on this classification. The system can now be trained as a supervised learning model with labeled data, and it can detect possible birth abnormalities with an accuracy of 96.2%. The machine learning model and result interpretation are integrated using a Python Flask framework on the backend. Additionally, expectant mothers can enter their age, AFP, HCG, and E3 levels using an easy-to- use frontend web interface. After that, the system makes use of the trained model to forecast the likelihood of birth abnormalities and offers informational materials regarding the triple marker test, safety measures, and possible hazards. This method uses machine learning to examine unlabeled data and anticipate possible birth abnormalities during pregnancy, providing a useful tool for medical professionals and expectant mothers alike.

articleTitle: Quality Evaluation System of Engineering Cost Consulting Services Based on COWA-Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper aims to construct a quality evaluation system for engineering cost consulting services to improve the scientificity and accuracy of these services. Firstly, through a review of relevant literature, the application prospects and significance of data mining and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation methods in the evaluation of engineering cost consulting service quality are introduced. Secondly, a multidimensional indicator system including service responsiveness, professionalism, reliability, and cost-effectiveness is constructed, and the weights of these indicators are determined using the COWA operator weighting method combined with data mining. Then, based on the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method, a quality evaluation model for engineering cost consulting services is established, considering both the weights of various indicators and the evaluation results. Finally, using a case study of a high-speed highway project, the effectiveness and feasibility of the model are verified. Empirical analysis shows that the evaluation system and model proposed in this paper have certain reference value and practicality in evaluating the quality of engineering cost consulting services.

articleTitle: Continuous Sign Language Recognition Using Leap Motion Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: A vital communication tool that connects persons with hearing and speech impairments worldwide is sign language. Sign language involves mostly hand movements plus face gestures, which are interpreted by recognizing these gestures to form meaningful sentences. In this study, we use two machine learning models: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Support Vector Machines (SVM), to predict signs. A dataset of 42 unique sign words and 28 sentences was used to train and evaluate our models. Our method uses depth sensors, like the Leap Motion gadget, to improve sign language recognition (SLR).Worldwide, sign language is an essential communication tool for people with speech and hearing impairments. Sign languages are primarily made up of hand gestures and facial expressions, and their meaning is communicated through precise gesture interpretation. Our models were trained on a dataset containing 42 distinct sign words and 28 sentences, achieving an accuracy of 90.35% for word prediction and 98.21 for sentence prediction. The LSTM model outperformed the SVM model, which had accuracies of 85.96% and 89.58% for words and sentences, respectively. By using depth sensors like the Leap Motion device, our approach aims to enhance sign language recognition (SLR).

articleTitle: Empathetic Analytics: Understanding Diabetes through AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This study paper investigates the use using Artificial Intelligence (AI) for diabetes diagnosis, specifically machine learning techniques to improve predictive accuracy. The study explores the AI model's performance measures using a broad dataset spanning many forms of diabetes, namely Type I, Type II, Type III, Type IV, or Type V. Precision, recall, or F1-score scores for each type of diabetes show consistently high levels of accuracy, ranging from 94.34% through 95.42%. In addition, support values show a strong representation of every diabetes class in the dataset, which adds to the algorithm's reliability. Furthermore, support proportions highlight an equitable distribution of data among diabetes kinds. In general, the macro, weighted, or micro accuracy ratings of roughly 94.84% demonstrate the AI model's competence in accurately diagnosing diabetes kinds. These findings emphasize the promise of AI-driven approaches to diabetes diagnosis, with intriguing implications to enhance patient care or healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Mapping the Distribution Pattern of Startups on Hilly Regions of Uttarakhand: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This research aims to analyze the distribution of startups within hilly regions all over the world in order to fill a gap in the literature that largely dominates urban and metropolitan spaces. Distribution of startups within geographically challenging areas like mountains has less deeply investigated dynamics, while those regions are nowadays increasingly recognized as engines of economic developments and innovations. This study therefore delves deeply into the insights on how businesses spread across a variety of hilly geographic spaces and across a variety of industry sectors, while also shedding light on their growth patterns. The study looks specifically at the influences put in place by governments and financial incentives; as well as through networking support and public initiatives towards encouraging more businesses to actively develop in these spaces.The research also identifies how these businesses managed to adapt and grow regardless of the challenges imposed by regions infrastructure and educational institutions using a quantitative approach. Important insights also emerge on how hilly regions are really potential hubs for new innovations and entrepreneurial enterprises.This research provides valuable perspectives for policymakers, investors, and other stakeholders who are striving to promote sustainable development and economic diversification in mountainous areas by expanding the concept of startup ecosystems beyond urban centres. The study's ultimate objective is to provide insights into strategies that can facilitate the expansion of businesses in hilly regions worldwide, thereby contributing to a more equitable and inclusive economic environment.

articleTitle: Oral Lesion Cell Segmentation and Classification using Convolution Neural Network Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Oral Cancer of the mouth kills millions of people, Oral cancer is better treated and more often survived when caught early. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have recently shown remarkable promise for cancer diagnosis and other medical image processing applications. In this study, we train deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect oral cancer early. The suggested approach makes use of a large database of pictures of the mouth and its cavities. Develop and refine a convolutional neural network (CNN) model using the use of radiographs, histology slides, and intraoral images. Oral carcinogenic tumours, both precancerous and malignant, may be identified and classified automatically using this approach. The process begins with picture pre-processing, continues with dataset supplementation for better model generalizability, and culminates in the use of complex neural networks for feature extraction and learning. Transfer learning methods modify previously taught models for this medical imaging task. The system’s performance, sensitivity, and accuracy are evaluated using a set of images that have pre-existing diagnoses. Deep learning CNNs were able to identify oral cancer with an efficiency and accuracy of 93.62%, according to the research. The trained model is a valuable tool for early cancer screening because of its high sensitivity and specificity. By automating the process, oral cancer may be detected and treated more quickly, which improves patient outcomes and decreases the disease burden.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Application in Lung Cancer Prediction: Insights from Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This research is intended to mark the accomplishment of a system designed and developed for the prediction of lung cancer, which will definitely be of great advantages to the doctors in identifying the probability of lung malignancies in a patient through computing clinical data. There are several considerations that are used in order to construct this system. The methodology includes five pivotal stages and originally fifteen significant clinical factors are taken under consideration: The variables were, age, gender, yellow_fingers, smoking_history, peer_pressure, anxiety, fatigue, allergies, chronic_disease, wheezing, alcohol, coughing, difficulties in swallowing, shortness of breath and chest pain. Cross validation was done using K-Fold to guarantee that the model was credible. However, since we had a rather imbalanced data set, performing conventional K-Fold cross-validation might pose some tendencies in the estimations. Hence, there was a need to make sure that the class distribution was maintained across all folds, and that’s why Stratified K-Fold cross-sectioning was used. This technique indicated that at one point, Gradient Boost & Decision Tree models were most accurate averaging 95.6%. But after integrating enough supervision and comparison, Random Forest proved to be the most accurate algorithm in the experiment with accuracy of 94.6%. This is the sort of model that will be equipped with technologically enhanced features for predicting lung cancer using advanced machine learning and data analysis methods. This feature of the system to accept other clinical data makes this systems a marvel in efficiency and increases the accuracy in the deterministic of lung cancer amongst people.

articleTitle: Investigating Mobile Phone Price Variability: A Quantile Regression Study of Hardware Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: A wide range of technical and design factors impact the complex phenomenon of mobile phone pricing. This research paper employs quantile regression at multiple quantiles to unravel the intricate relationships between mobile phone prices and key independent variables, including RAM, rear camera, resolution, internal memory, battery capacity, and others. By analyzing different quantiles of the price distribution, this research illuminates how these variables have varying effects among price points, revealing subtleties hidden in more conventional linear regression methods. The findings provide a comprehensive understanding of the impact of various features on mobile phone prices and reveal distinct patterns in price sensitivity at different quantiles. Compared to traditional OLS regression, quantile regression is conducted at the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, and 90th percentiles to identify how certain specifications drive premium pricing while others exert more pronounced effects on budget models. This knowledge can guide pricing strategies for manufacturers, inform consumer choices, and offer insights into the evolving landscape of the mobile phone market. Our research provides a more nuanced perspective on pricing dynamics in the mobile industry, which will ultimately help stakeholders make better decisions and position their products as technology and consumer preferences continue to diversify.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Early Diabetes Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer a significant advantage in early diabetes prediction, enabling proactive healthcare interventions that can mitigate the risk of complications. In this review, we explore various AI-driven approaches to predict diabetes, focusing on a project that implemented multiple ML models, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Gradient Boosting, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression. The KNN model demonstrated the best overall performance, achieving an accuracy score of 75%, as evidenced by other metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC, leading to its deployment in a real-world application using Flask, a lightweight web framework. This deployment allows for real-time diabetes risk assessment, offering healthcare providers and patients an accessible tool for early diabetes prediction. However, the project also identified challenges related to data quality and model bias, underscoring the importance of addressing these limitations for broader adoption of AI-driven healthcare tools. This review concludes by discussing future directions for AI in healthcare, including potential improvements to diabetes prediction models and ethical considerations. The outcomes suggest that AI can play a crucial role in managing chronic diseases like diabetes, offering a pathway toward improved patient outcomes through early detection and personalized treatment.

articleTitle: Optimizing Healthcare Accessibility and Effectiveness through the Implementation of AI Solutions for Remote Patient Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This study investigates the optimization of healthcare accessibility and effectiveness by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) solutions within Internet of Things (IoT) systems for remote patient monitoring. Embracing a holistic approach, we deploy medical sensors, including temperature, pressure, heart rate, and oxygen sensors, to collect patients' continuous health metrics (vital signs). These sensed data are then transmitted to an Arduino controller, responsible for managing data communication with the cloud infrastructure using a Wi-Fi module that facilitates data storage and analysis. Stored data are accessed by authorized healthcare professionals, who exploit machine learning models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Logistic Regression (LR) and Decision Tree (DT), to forecast patients' health outcome in advance using the sensed data. A rigorous evaluation demonstrated the IoT system's effectiveness, based on testing with sensed data from ten patients over a month, where 70% of the data were used for training the models, and the rest for testing. The proposed IoT system demonstrates the success; ANN exhibited the highest accuracy at 97.88%, followed by LR at 93.43%, and DT at 91.20%. Precision, recall, and F1 scores further validated the models' ability to predict health outcome accurately. Evaluation of the accuracy and loss curves showed the convergence of the models towards optimal performance. This study contributes to remote healthcare monitoring and provides a promising IoT paradigm for realizing ubiquitous remote monitoring, optimized healthcare effectiveness, and patient outcome through AI-enabled IoT systems.

articleTitle: Privacy-preserving federated learning in healthcare: Fundamentals, state of the art and prospective research directions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Recent collaborations in medical diagnostic systems are based on data private collaborative learning using Federated Learning (FL). In this approach, multiple organizations train a machine-learning model at the same time eventually leading to global model generation. This paper reviews the fundamentals of FL and its evolution path in Healthcare. The objective of this review is to scope a wide variety of healthcare applications in FL. Exactly what research direction is moving in interesting for research communities to guide their future course. This review uniquely focuses on examining numerous FL-based healthcare implementations, detailing their core methodologies and performance metrics, which, to our knowledge, have not been previously available. Privacy-preserving collaborative distributed learning through federated learning in healthcare enhances research collaborations, thereby resulting in better-performing models. This comprehensive review will act as a valuable reference for researchers exploring new FL applications in the healthcare domain.

articleTitle: Antenna optimization based on genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In modern communication systems, optimizing antenna phase is crucial for improving signal quality and reducing interference. Genetic algorithms (GAs) are frequently employed for this purpose due to their ability to avoid local minima and identify global solutions within large search spaces. This survey provides a comprehensive review of existing research on antenna phase optimization using genetic algorithms. It examines the strengths and weaknesses of current techniques, analyzes various methodologies and their outcomes reported in the literature, and critically compares the performance of genetic algorithms with other optimization methods. This survey aims to guide future research and serve as an extensive resource for engineers and researchers in the field.

articleTitle: Dynamic Face Tracking and Route Prediction Across Distributed Camera Network Using MobileFaceNet and Partial Trajectory Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In an era where security and surveillance are paramount, this paper presents a comprehensive framework for real-time face recognition and pedestrian trajectory prediction, leveraging the capabilities of MobileFaceNet and a Partial Trajectory Matching Algorithm. The system is designed to enhance surveillance and monitoring by integrating accurate face recognition with predictive path analysis. Known face images and historical trajectory data are utilized to recognize individuals and forecast their movement patterns. The framework processes live video feeds, detecting and identifying faces in real time. Upon identification, it segments and matches the pedestrian’s trajectory against historical data to predict future movements. Performance is evaluated using metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach in improving situational awareness and response times in security applications.

articleTitle: Optimization CT images using GANs: Stroke context in Senegal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Generative adversarial networks (GAN) are an emerging technology in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). It is an unsupervised learning framework that involves automatically learning a model from input data to produce a synthetic output that closely resembles the original input. GANs create datasets by making copies of false outputs based on specific inputs. GANs allow machines to generate unique content that is different from human-generated data. GANs are widely used in various image-related fields, such as image-to-text conversion, next-generation faces, high-resolution image conversion, etc. The general growth of artificial intelligence and its medical applications is increasing the efficiency of the healthcare system for patients who need rapid care. Chronic diseases, especially stroke, are now the leading cause of death worldwide. Diagnosis of stroke is often based on imaging techniques such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, CT scans are more common and readily available in many African hospitals, especially in Senegal. However, the need for rapid image interpretation of stroke is sometimes problematic due to variable image quality, highlighting the need for improvements to achieve better image quality. This article focuses on improving the resolution of CT images, a commonly used method in medical imaging. However, obtaining a high-quality CT scan often requires lengthy wait times and the use of limited laboratory equipment. In addition, radioactive radiation poses health risks and results in poorer image quality. Super-resolution GAN has the potential to solve this problem. Super-resolution is a method of generating high-resolution images from low-resolution images. We use the input CT dataset to generate higher quality images while keeping parameters unchanged. We found that using ResNet with GANs produced higher quality images than the original input images.

articleTitle: Webcam-Guided Gesture-Controlled Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of a gesture-controlled robotic arm that is navigated with the help of a webcam and OpenCV-enabled real-time hand tracking. Embedded with OpenCV’s hand tracking module, the system successfully identifies the hand landmarks from the live camera captured hand movement of the user. By the current state of each finger, the state is represented by a string format that includes the $ symbol and number (such as$00010) that is transmitted to an Arduino Uno board, the robotic arm can move its fingers up or down. Control of the flows of the movement of the robotic arm is done using the Arduino Uno whereby the servo motors receive signals to move 0 or 180 degrees. This is mainly due to the efficiency, precision and short latency of the suggested system which makes it novel that gives the user a simple graphics interface to control robotic arms without necessity to know programming or have specific hardware. This technology provides an effective solution in robotic manipulation and presents the enormous potential to enhance HRI in different application areas.

articleTitle: HealthMate: A Comprehensive Mobile Application for Personalized Health and Fitness Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The worldwide health picture is transforming towards proactive self-care and tailored wellness solutions, driven by technological breakthroughs. In response to the increased frequency of lifestyle-related diseases and mental health concerns, we aim to create a comprehensive mobile application that employs machine learning and image processing techniques. This program enables users to make more informed decisions regarding their health and develop healthier living habits. The software aims to address harmful behaviors by providing personalized support through features like food analysis, calorie estimation, and mood tracking. It democratizes access to individualized health services using machine learning and image processing technologies. The research explores the convergence of these technologies for a healthier lifestyle, ultimately contributing to a happier society through individualized guidance.

articleTitle: Natural Language Processing Approach for Fake News Detection Using Metaheuristics Optimized Extreme Gradient Boosting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The problem of fake news can be dangerous, as widely spread misinformation can cause serious physical and psychological harm. In the age of digitization and artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning methods, which are able to generated synthetic text, being able to distinguish between real and fake news has become even greater challenge. Therefore, this research proposes a metaheuristics optimized machine learning (ML) approach with natural language processing (NLP) application for detecting fake news. The main classification model that was used is the eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), which was tuned by the modified variable neighborhood search (VNS) algorithm. The NLP technique that was applied to transform text into the meaningful form for ML is the term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF). The performance of the VNS-tuned XGBoost was evaluated and compared with other cutting edge metaheuristics, where the proposed method obtained superior performance.

articleTitle: Towards Seamless Integration of AI-Driven Agents in Video Games: Techniques, Challenges, and Implications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The integration of AI-driven agents in video games enhances gameplay automation and player experience. This research leverages a custom-trained object detection model op-timized for low-latency performance to automate tasks such as aiming and uses dead reckoning for player movement prediction. An Arduino-based system is implemented for real-time command transmission, facilitating interaction between the AI agent and the game environment. Experiments demonstrate precise aiming and responsive gameplay, showcasing the potential to improve player experience and automate testing processes. Ethical considerations regarding AI deployment in competitive gaming emphasize the importance of fair play and integrity. Our findings advance AI technology in gaming and offer valuable insights for industry stakeholders.

articleTitle: ACIDA-IA: Addressing Class Imbalance Does not Always Improve Accuracy: a Study of Bayesian Networks for Predicting Preeclampsia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Real-world applications often deal with class-unbalanced data sets, especially in the medical field. Machine learning (ML) algorithms that learn predictive models can be affected by unbalanced data. This research presents the impact of oversampling and undersampling techniques on the learning of Bayesian classification models that predict the probability of developing preeclampsia. Oversampling and undersampling techniques that work with categorical and numerical variables will be considered given the characteristics of our dataset. Specifically, random oversampling (OVER), random undersampling (UNDER), random oversampling examples (ROSE), and synthetic minority oversampling techniques for nominal and continuous data (SMOTE-NC) are considered. The results show no improvement in accuracy percentages when dealing with class imbalances in the training data set. However, the models that dealt with class imbalance had a more balanced result in correctly classifying positive and negative cases of preeclampsia in the test dataset. We can conclude that although oversampling and under-sampling techniques can be used to deal with imbalanced training datasets before building prediction models, an improvement in the accuracy of the models is not always guaranteed, although it certainly improves (in most cases) the sensitivity and specificity percentages in a binary classification problem such as the one considered in this manuscript.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Security: A Study on Hybrid Intrusion Detection Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This electronic document is a “live” template and already defines the components of your paper [title, text, heads, etc.] in its style sheet. *CRITICAL: Do Not Use Symbols, Special Characters, Footnotes, or Math in Paper Title or Abstract. (Abstract) The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has led to increased vulnerability to cyber intrusion threats like malware and denial-of-service attacks, which can severely impact system availability, reliability, and trustworthiness. Existing intrusion detection systems often rely on single environments for training models, limiting their real-world versatility against evolving attacks spanning diverse systems. To address these challenges, this study proposes an integrated deep learning approach that combines heterogeneous datasets using representation learning based on stacked convolutional autoencoders and distribution alignment. This approach aims to improve model generalization and enable the detection of threats across various IoT environments. The proposed method employs hybrid convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to perform robust binary and multi-class classification. By analyzing spatial context and sequential traffic dynamics, the model can distinguish normal functionality from different attack types. Extensive evaluation on the NSL-KDD and SDN-5-IoT intrusion detection benchmarks demonstrates over 99% accuracy in detecting both known and zero-day attacks. Comparisons with standalone deep architectures indicate consistent performance gains from the synergistic fusion of spatial and temporal modeling. The proposed approach advances adaptive threat intelligence for securing real-world IoT ecosystems against evolving cyber threats. The integration of heterogeneous datasets and the combination of CNN and LSTM architectures enable the model to learn more generalized representations of network traffic patterns, enhancing its ability to detect intrusions across diverse IoT systems. This research contributes to the development of robust and versatile intrusion detection systems that can adapt to the ever-changing landscape of cyber threats in the IoT domain, ultimately improving the security and reliability of connected devices and networks.

articleTitle: Solving 100-Digit Challenge using Q-learning inspired Differential Evolution Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The 100-digit challenge requires solving ten complex optimization problems of the CEC 2019 benchmark test suite with the precision of ten digits. The challenge does not recommend any constraint on the maximum number of function evaluations or iterations. The rationale behind this relaxation is to reward accuracy over rapid convergence. This research proposes a Q-learning inspired Differential Evolution (DE) (QLiDE) algorithm to solve the 100-digit challenge. A Q-learning framework consisting of state-space and action-space is set up using the fitness vector and a pool of DE mutation strategies, respectively. The mutation strategies in the pool are rewarded based on their cumulative performance, and the reward values are utilized as feedback signals for updating the Q-values. The proposed algorithm achieves the score of 93 out of 100 and secures an overall rank 3 over all other algorithms applied for solving the 100-digit challenge, till date.

articleTitle: Semantic Similarity Analysis using FastText
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Accurately capturing semantic similarities between words is crucial for various natural language processing (NLP) applications, such as information retrieval and text summarization. Word embeddings, that represent words as dense vectors, have proven effective in this task. This study investigates the impact of dimensionality in association with data on the quality of FastText word embeddings and their ability to capture semantic similarities. Different FastText models (SkipGram and CBOW) are trained on a large Wikipedia corpus, with varying dimensionalities and are evaluated as per the Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) benchmark dataset using the Pearson Correlation Coefficient. Our findings provide insights into the model training time and performance, highlighting the strengths and limitations of different configurations, which helps in selecting appropriate dimensionality based on the desired balance between accuracy and computational efficiency. This research advances the understanding of the role of dimensionality with respect to data in word embedding models and their application to semantic similarity tasks, informing the development of robust NLP techniques for accurate language understanding.

articleTitle: Extensive Data Preprocessing and Exploratory Data Analysis for House Price Prediction using Machine Learning and Deep Learning with an Introduction to AutoML Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Houses contribute to one of the most essential needs of every human and house prices play a very important role in everyone’s life. House Price prediction has been one of the crucial topics in the real estate industry. This paper focuses on data preprocessing techniques which are carried out using dataset containing the house prices of the Ames City in United States. It covers the entire journey right from Data collection to Data Preprocessing and Data Analysis to Prediction using various Models. In this paper, Machine learning, Deep Learning and Auto ML techniques are applied to study historical property transactions in Ames to find useful models for both house buyers and sellers. The Models we test as a part of this paper are Random Forest Regression, Ridge Regression, Lasso Regression, (SVR) Support Vector Regression, XGBoost (which is an optimized distributed gradient boosting library) and ANN (Artificial Neural Networks). While ANN and Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) represent the forefront of machine learning, our exploration demonstrates that classical ML models remain indispensable across various domains. Our findings also demonstrate that the effectiveness of any machine learning model is highly dependent on comprehensive and rigorous data preprocessing.
