articleTitle: Integrated Airflow and Temperature Monitoring System for Enhanced Underground Mine Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Beneath the surface lies a huge challenge and opportunity, the underground environment of coal mines. This subterranean world, where human endeavor meets the rawness of nature, is a melting pot of industry, technology, and resource extraction. Coal mining is an industry deeply rooted in history, dating back centuries to the earliest human civilizations. It represents an effort to use the Earth’s ancient energy reserves, stored as carbon-rich coal, for heating, industrial processes, and power generation. Mining in the underground environment presents a unique set of challenges and risks that require constant vigilance and innovative safety measures. This article proposes a continuous, seamless monitoring system that transmits the underground mine data to the surface station which requires advanced arrangements to emerge from the impediments of routine hardware, which falls flat to supply real-time knowledge. Next, attention is drawn to a cutting-edge system fitted with an ESP32 microcontroller, temperature, CO, methane, and airflow sensors, and LoRa for data transfer. Thresholds and buzzers have been set for alarming, which alerts workers at the right moment. A novel TinyML-based anomaly detection system that integrates with an Arduino cloud and MQTT broker. By implementing cutting-edge techniques and imposing historical constraints, this revolutionary strategy ultimately increases the safety of under- ground mines where there will be a significant improvement in safety monitoring technology.

articleTitle: Visualizing Real-Time Predictions in Action Recognition Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Our study focuses on action recognition, a crucial component of computer vision with applications in surveillance, HCI, and autonomous systems. Leveraging the UCF50 dataset, a repository of real-world action videos, we embark on a comprehensive analysis. Our approach centers on refining deep learning models to address the unique challenges posed by UCF50. We introduce innovations to well-established architectures, prioritizing precision, robustness, and generalization. Given the dataset's diversity, housing 50 action categories with varying lighting, camera angles, and occlusions, our models focus on capturing intricate spatiotemporal patterns. Through rigorous testing, our models exhibit significant improvements in action identification accuracy, surpassing current benchmarks. A meticulous exploration of model behavior sheds light on strengths and limitations, especially in decoding subtle temporal cues and fine-grained actions. We also highlight the importance of addressing dataset biases and the imperative for more robust algorithms. Our research not only advances the understanding of deep learning's potential in action recognition but also underscores the UCF50 dataset's pivotal role in model development. By sharing our insights and methodology, we aim to catalyze further exploration in dataset creation, model refinement, and computational efficiency, pushing the boundaries of action recognition within the computer vision domain.

articleTitle: Object Identification Using Generative AI: An Application of Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The exponential growth of image data in recent years, driven by the widespread adoption of digital photography and the proliferation of social media platforms, presents a pressing challenge: how to efficiently identify objects within this vast sea of visual information. Traditional methods of object identification often struggle to cope with the scale and complexity of modern image datasets. Generative AI, a subset of machine learning, focuses on creating models that can generate data resembling real examples from a given domain. The most prominent approaches within Generative AI which are Variational Autoencoders and Generative Adversarial Networks have shown remarkable capabilities in generating images which are realistic and capturing complex data distributions, making them promising candidates for improving object identification tasks. Object detection has undergone significant evolution in algorithms, aiming to enhance both accuracy and speed. Thanks to the relentless numerous researcher’s effort, deep learning algorithms have swiftly advanced, resulting in improved object detection capabilities. These advancements find widespread application in various domains such as medical imaging, pedestrian detection, self-driving cars, and face detection, robotics among others, thereby streamlining tasks previously reliant on human effort. Given the expansive nature of the field and the plethora of state-of-the-art algorithms, comprehensively covering them all at once proves to be a daunting endeavor. This paper seeks to provide a foundational overview on the methodologies of object detection, focusing on the detection stages. In the realm of two-stage detectors, algorithms like RCNN, Fast RCNN, and Faster RCNN are explored, prioritizing accuracy. Conversely, one-stage detectors such as YOLO versions emphasize speed.

articleTitle: Almond Quality Assessment using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Almonds, scientifically referred to as Prunus dulcis, hold a significant position as a globally favored nut variety. Ensuring consistent almond quality is paramount in the food industry to meet stringent standards and fulfill consumer expectations. The manual hand-picking methods for categorizing Almond varieties are time-consuming and inefficient which would result in visual fatigue. Hence, the proposed study introduces an innovative approach leveraging deep learning methodologies to automate the assessment of almond quality based on RGB images. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), specifically the VGG16 and ResNet50 models are deployed to analyze almond images based on features such as size, shape, and texture. The experimentation analysis is carried out using a self-built dataset encompassing diverse almond varieties such as Shell, Mamra Type 1, Mamra Type 2, Mamra Type 3, Mamra Type 4, and Senora. It is observed that VGG16 surpasses the ResNet50model in performanceby achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 96%, while RESNET50 achieves 89% accuracy. By accurately classifying the almond varieties, it can ensure quality standards are met in the food processing industry.

articleTitle: An Efficient Crypto Based Ransomware Prevention Method in Android Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: A relatively new kind of intrusion attack called ransomware aims to demand a ransom from its target. Ransomware attacks are carried out by cybercriminals to financially affect victims by damaging their gadgets. Due to Android’s widespread use worldwide, assaults on smartphones using this operating system are growing exponentially. While there are many different kinds of ransomware attacks, this article mainly concentrates on crypto-ransomware as, once the victim’s files are encrypted, it renders data irretrievable. We provided a thorough examination based on machine learning crypto-ransomware detection techniques in this study. This detection must be successful to stop the attack from achieving its objective. In this work, we provide a classification scheme for the security level of crypto-ransomware for detection as well as prevention. This framework includes data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction and selection, or classification, and the application of multiple machine learning techniques. We assessed the accuracy, recall, F1-score, and precision scores using a single Android ransomware dataset. The comparison findings show that the Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifier performs better than competing approaches across all performance metrics, with a 99.5% accuracy rate in detecting crypto Android ransomware. Unlike most previous studies that provide an analysis of crypto-ransomware, this is a thorough assessment that focuses on detection techniques.

articleTitle: Enhanced CNN-SVM Fusion for In-Depth Facial Acne Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to present and access a comprehensive analysis of an advanced facial acne classification method that is focused on machine learning. Hormonal acne, pustules, papules, cysts, blackheads (open comedones), and whiteheads (closed comedones) were all included in the dataset that was used to train and evaluate the algorithm. Accuracy, recall, and F1-Score provide evidence that the model correctly recognizes a variety of acne types, with scores ranging from 93.98% to 95.86%. Other evaluation metrics also suggest that the model displays this accuracy and efficiency. As an additional point of interest, the support percentage demonstrates how samples are spread within each acne class, hence demonstrating the balanced distribution of classes within the dataset. The model demonstrated that it was very accurate, obtaining a total score of 98% for its performance. In addition, aggregate performance metrics such as micro, weighted, and macro averages provide further evidence that the algorithm is capable of providing a diagnosis of acne that is both accurate and trustworthy across all types of acne. The research contributes to the development of automated systems for detecting acne on the face, and dermatologists may find it beneficial to utilize the data acquired to improve their ability to diagnose and treat patients who suffer from facial acne and health issues.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Predicting Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson's Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: A chronic neurodegenerative disorder affecting the motor system is called Parkinson's disease. Cell degeneration results from it over time as it advances slowly. This is one of the most prevalent diseases in society and is difficult to diagnose. The body experiences both motor and non-motor deficits (such as smell and speech) as a result of a dopamine cell shortage in the brain. Speech problems are common among Parkinson's sufferers, as is well documented. When compared to normal individuals, speech signals from Parkinson's sufferers show notable changes. This study proposes to use voice signals' acoustic properties to classify Parkinson's diseases using a deep learning-based approach. First, a genetic algorithm is used for the auditory characteristics in order to identify useful aspects. The ReliefF feature selection approach and the genetic algorithm's performance are also contrasted. The second phase involves feeding the chosen characteristics into the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture that has been created. An accuracy of 93.29% is attained without feature selection, whereas 97.62% is attained with feature selection.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of VNFs and Service Function Chaining in an Edge Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Network Function Virtualization (NFV) and Service Function Chaining (SFC) are developing concepts that are gaining acceptance in modern networking. These paradigms were developed in response to the increasing complexity of network services and the need to create more efficient, adaptable, and scalable methods of delivering these services. The chaining of network services across several domains is made possible by SFC as an extension of NFV. SFC entails the sequential grouping of network functions to form a chain of functions that are applied to incoming packets. This allows network managers to customize network services and implement sophisticated capabilities like deep packet inspection, load balancing, and firewall in a scalable and efficient manner. SFC, on the other hand, is an NFC extension that enables the chaining of network services over various domains. This enables network operators to design advanced networks, without having to rely on complex and inefficient manual configuration. SFC has been adopted in a wide range of applications and use cases, including cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT), and software-defined networking (SDN). These paradigms have the potential to provide more agile and flexible network architectures. For obtaining efficient chaining that takes the minimum latency delay possible to service the virtual functions, we have used Q-Learning Method Reinforcement based machine learning. We have also considered the case in which multiple VNFs are present in MECs. By implementing this we obtained that using Q-Learning, we can keep the state of previously chosen MEC for the same SFC so that the same optimal path will be selected. Additionally, we can see that the graph for computing time for the SFC request, which has a longer VNF, won’t show a steep increase.

articleTitle: Enhanced Forging Process Improvement: Utilizing CNN-SVM Hybrid Models for Precision and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The abstract presents a detailed investigation into the classification and assessment of different surface defects observed in forging procedures, employing a hybrid CNN-SVM model within a machine learning structure. The primary objective of the research is to evaluate the model's efficiency in identifying and classifying nine specific types of forging defects: unfilled section or underfill, scale pits, cold shut, flakes, surface cracking, die shift, residual stress in forging, and incomplete forging penetration. Key performance indicators such as precision, recall, and F1-score are employed to gauge the model's accuracy across these defect categories. The forging flaw classification model has 95.94% accuracy on 10,131 pictures. The outcomes reveal consistently high-performance levels, with precision values varying from 92.04% to 98.10% and recall values from 92.56% to 96.67%. The model attains an overall macro-average F1-score of 95.93%, indicating its strong capability to manage diverse defect types with precision. Moreover, the study emphasizes the significance of support proportion and weighted averages in interpreting the model's performance concerning the dataset's size and class distribution. The support proportion, which ranges from 0.12 to 0.13 across defect types, mirrors the dataset's balanced representation of various forging flaws, ensuring thorough model training and assessment. In conclusion, the results underscore the effectiveness of the CNN-SVM hybrid model in automated defect identification during forging processes, highlighting its potential to enhance quality control procedures by accurately recognizing and categorizing defects. This investigation provides valuable insights into advancing machine learning applications in industrial environments, to enhance manufacturing efficiency and product quality through advanced defect recognition technologies.

articleTitle: Integrated CNN-SVM System for Accurate Identification of Narrow Strip Defects in Sheet Metal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The research utilized a CNN-SVM model to classify metal defects, specifically focusing on Coil Set, Crossbow, and Torsion. The results showed that the model performed exceptionally well, with precision, recall, and F1-score consistently exceeding 98%. These metrics demonstrate the model's ability to accurately identify and categorize different types of metal defects, which is crucial for quality control in manufacturing. The CNN-SVM model for metal defect classification was evaluated using a dataset of 10,940 images, resulting in an impressive overall accuracy of 98.35%. The dataset used for training and evaluation had a balanced distribution of support values for each class, ensuring comprehensive coverage of all defect types. This balanced representation enhances the model's ability to generalize and perform reliably in various industrial scenarios. With an overall accuracy of 99%, the model excels in distinguishing between different defect types with high precision and reliability. This accuracy is supported by Macro, Weighted, and Micro Average metrics, which confirm the model's consistent performance across different evaluation methods. The Weighted Average F1-score of 98.35% further highlights the model's effectiveness in achieving both classification accuracy and proportional support distribution across classes. In conclusion, this study emphasizes the effectiveness of the CNN-SVM model in detecting and classifying metal defects, offering significant potential for improving quality assurance processes in manufacturing. These findings contribute to the advancement of automated defect detection systems, leading to increased operational efficiency, cost reduction, and improved product quality across various industrial sectors. Future research can focus on refining the model and expanding its application to broader manufacturing contexts to maximize its impact and utility.

articleTitle: Process Automation for Enhanced Supply Chain Management with Internet of Things (IoT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: the internet of things (IoT) is a swiftly developing technology that allows physical objects to attach and alternate records with each other and with the net. With its ability to digitize and automate techniques, IoT has a tremendous effect on supply chain control (SCM) with the aid of supplying actual-time facts and increasing efficiency. To further beautify SCM, the integration of IoT with process automation can optimize operations and enhance selection-making. Process automation is using era to streamline and automate manual procedures, ensuring better accuracy, quicker execution, and reduced hard work fees. Via combining IoT and manner automation, the supply chain can take advantage of sensors, records analytics, and device studying to accumulate and analyze real-time data, make predictions, and automate tasks. This allows for a more agile and responsive supply chain, wherein tactics may be adjusted in real-time primarily based on demand, delivery, or other outside elements.one of the key benefits of manner automation with IoT is stepped forward stock management. Sensors can sing inventory ranges in actual-time, triggering automated reorder requests whilst stock tiers reach a sure threshold. This removes the want for guide inventory tests and guarantees that important objects are constantly available, decreasing the danger of stock outs.

articleTitle: Analytical Framework for Comprehensive Classification of Female Alopecia: CNN-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The research findings on hair loss classification using a machine learning model are summarized in the abstract and detailed in Table 1. The model achieved high precision values between 95.24% and 97.56%, accurately identifying each type of hair loss (Type I to Type IV). Recall values ranged from 95.62% to 97.38%, showing the model's ability to capture positive instances effectively within each category for reliable medical diagno stics . F1 scores remained consistently strong at 96.07% to 96.89%, indicating a balanced performance crucial for robust classification. Based on 10,360 photos, the algorithm classifies hair loss phases with 96.52% accuracy.Support values indicate dataset sizes for each hair loss type , demonstrating the model 's effectiveness in handling varying amounts of data. With an overall accuracy of 98 % , the model reliably categorized hair loss stages , showcasing its potential in clinical settings to assist dermatologists in diagnosis and treatment planning . In summary, the study highlights how machine learning enhances diagnostic accuracy for different hair loss conditions , leading to personalized treatment approaches based on specific types and severities. These findings advance medical diagnostics and patient care in dermatology , ultimately improving outcomes and quality of life for those affected by hair loss.

articleTitle: Order Visibility: Supply chain order milestone prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Primarily, the tools used for Supply planning are off-the-shelf products and ERP software with inbuilt capabilities. However, these tools are not customizable or entirely accessible to control and respond to changes in a quick manner. In the Healthcare manufacturing industry, volatility in the supply chain has adverse consequences. Lack of Order visibility leads to poor production planning, inefficient inventory, transport and distribution handling, poor mobilization of teams for ground support, poor customer satisfaction, and late value realization. This paper proposes a machine learning-based prediction model to predict a delivery date for a new Made-to-order medical equipment delivery. The machine learning model attempts to predict timelines with minimal features that are easier to explain, and scalable, and reduces the need to reconcile the approach and results with traditional enterprise systems, planning suites, and optimization software.

articleTitle: SleepEEG: An Automated Sleep Scoring System Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Sleep scoring, or categorizing sleep scores from EEG signals, is an important step in sleep medicine for detecting sleep disorders. Traditional manual scoring methods are time-consuming and subjective, encouraging automated solutions to be developed. In this study, we offer SleepEEG, an automated sleep grading system based on deep learning algorithms. Our model is trained using a huge dataset of annotated EEG recordings to learn the complicated patterns associated with various sleep stages. SleepEEG, a novel automated sleep scoring system based on deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), is presented. It analyzes electroencephalogram (EEG) data to classify sleep stages accurately. SleepEEG aims to improve clinical efficiency and patient outcomes through automation. The system achieves a test-balanced accuracy of 90.04% and a Cohen's kappa of 0.8705, demonstrating high agreement with human experts. Future directions include exploring multimodal data fusion and personalized modeling for enhanced sleep stage analysis. The article explores future options for addressing sleep stage scoring issues, such as multimodal data fusion and tailored-modeling. Automated sleep scoring detection broadens our understanding of sleep patterns, problems, and health.

articleTitle: Prediction of Path-loss Model for Millimeter Wave Communication using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Path loss represents a crucial element affecting the positioning of base stations within cellular networks. Consequently, a novel approach presented in the research for estimating signal attenuation in high-frequency wireless communication, specifically in millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication. The utilization of mmWave communication harbors the potential to enhance wireless data rates significantly owing to its expansive bandwidth. Nonetheless, it encounters impediments as the atmosphere can readily obstruct and diminish signals at these frequencies. A deep learning and artificial intelligence methodology was employed to address these obstacles. An extensive and varied dataset compiled, encompassing measurements derived from mmWave channels, environmental particulars, and signal attenuation data. This dataset encompassed diverse scenarios such as urban areas, suburban regions, and indoor settings, thus enabling the model to function effectively across varying contexts. Comprehensive data refinement and organization procedures established to prepare the dataset for the training of advanced learning models. Various types of neural networks, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) investigated to ensure the model's ability to interpret the complex patterns within the data. Thorough testing conducted to validate the model's proficiency in accurately predicting signal attenuation across different scenarios. The outcomes demonstrated the superior performance of the deep learning model compared to conventional approaches, displaying its adaptability to diverse environments and underscoring its utility in the planning and deployment of mmWave communication networks. In summary, this study furnishes a valuable instrument for creating efficient and dependable mmWave communication systems capable of facilitating high-speed data transmission in various real-world contexts.

articleTitle: Advancing Metallurgical Practices: Predictive Modeling for Defect Detection using CNN-Random Forest Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The abstract summarizes the findings of a study that focused on implementing a deep learning model for automated detection of metallurgical defects in industrial environments. The objective of this research is to improve quality assurance processes in response to the demands of Industry 4.0. The study evaluates the performance of the model using precision, recall, and F1-score metrics across various defect classes, including Segregation, Laminations, Flaws, Cold Shuts, Hot Tears, Gas Porosity, Surface Oxidation, Blowholes, Inclusions, and Hydrogen Embrittlement. The model was able to correctly identify 88.91% of the 12,259 pictures in the collection. The key findings indicate that the model achieves high precision values in most defect categories, with Flaws achieving the highest precision at 97.42%. This suggests that the model has a low rate of false positives in identifying defects. Additionally, Hot Tears demonstrated the highest recall at 96.70%, indicating the model's ability to effectively detect instances of this particular defect type. The F1-scores, which consider both precision and recall, range from 93.29% to 96.68%, confirming the model's balanced performance in accurately classifying defects. In general, the weighted average metrics of precision (95.46%), recall (95.44%), and F1-score (95.44%) demonstrate the model's consistent and reliable performance across all defect classes. These results highlight the potential of the model to significantly enhance manufacturing quality control processes by automating defect detection. This automation has the potential to improve production efficiency, reduce operational costs associated with manual inspection, and ensure higher standards of product quality in metallurgical industries. This study contributes to the advancement of quality assurance methodologies by utilizing deep learning techniques to address complex challenges in defect detection.

articleTitle: Advanced Attention Capsule Network with Curved Wavelet Attention for Illuminating Low-Light Capsule Endoscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Capsule endoscopy has transformed medical imaging with its non-invasive approach to visualize the gastrointestinal tract. However, challenges persist in low-light conditions, impacting diagnostic accuracy. This paper introduces the Advanced Attention Capsule Network (AACNet), fortified with curved wavelet attention blocks, leveraging dynamic curved parameter estimation, feature rescaling, and strategic pooling. By incorporating Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Inverse Wavelet Transform (IWT), and sigmoid activation, AACNet addresses low-light deficits in capsule endoscopy. This research explores the model's efficiency in handling varying object sizes through a spatial pyramid pooling layer. Channel attention modules and a dynamic channel attention module refine feature representation, enhancing the model's ability to discern intricate details within curved structures. The multi-level capsule network captures hierarchical relationships among features, contributing to a comprehensive solution for enhanced medical imaging. AACNet demonstrates remarkable results in achieving 85% accuracy across diverse anatomical classes like foreign body, lymphangiectasia, ampulla, and fresh blood. Precision values (85%) highlight AACNet's precision in minimizing false positives. Variable recall values showcase the model's adaptability, capturing true positives in distinct scenarios. F1 scores emphasize AACNet's effective balance between precision and recall, which is crucial for robust diagnostics. Specificity values underscore AACNet's accuracy in identifying negative instances.

articleTitle: IoT-enabled Asset Monitoring and Optimization Railway System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The paper discusses an IoT-based railway management system for detecting cracks on railway tracks, monitoring platform availability, fire detection and suppression, train movement control, and automatic level crossing gate operations. The proposed system integrates various sensors (IR, ultrasonic, camera, fire), Arduino microcontrollers, DC motors, relays, Zigbee communication, and image processing techniques. The crack detection module employs IR sensors, ultrasonic sensors, and image processing algorithms to identify cracks or obstacles on the tracks. The platform monitoring module uses IR sensors to track platform occupancy and enable efficient train scheduling. The fire detection module incorporates fire sensors and activates water pumps, sprinklers, and emergency train compartment detachment mechanisms. The train movement module utilizes DC motors for precise acceleration, deceleration, and movement control. The level- crossing module automatically opens and closes gates based on train arrival and departure times. The system provides real- time communication and alerts through Node MCU and Zigbee technology. The article draws attention to the severe damage done by track-related accidents, which are among India's top causes of loss of life and property. The paper stresses how vital it is that railways are safe. This paper talks about the various problems with the Indian railway network and why there is a need for an efficient technology for track fault detection. Moreover, this paper’s focus extends to the more innovative approaches, including UAVs fitted with cameras and LiDAR sensors for aerial inspection of rails, new materials for improved track lifespan and strength, implementation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices enabling real-time information-gathering and robotic systems for autonomous maintenance duties on tracks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Public Safety through Face Mask Detection using Xception Deep Learning Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Recent developments in controlling the ongoing epidemic include the widespread use of face masks. This creates an urgent need for precise and fast analytical systems for face mask detection to ensure public safety from viral infectious diseases. This paper proposes an optimal and innovative mask detection method based on the Xception deep learning model to automatically identify faces, whether masked or not. The performance was tested utilizing an effective dataset of 11,792 pictures, segregated into two categories: With Mask and Without Mask. The model was trained with the Adam optimizer and binary cross-entropy loss function to achieve the desired performance. As a result, the model trained on the training dataset demonstrated a high accuracy of 98.79% on the test dataset. Additionally, the results revealed high precision, recall, and F1 scores, all of which were above 0.99 for the two categories. This is due to a high level of precision and recall at multiple average data points but low errors in classification. A confusion matrix and a classification report were developed to demonstrate the comprehensive models' performance. Therefore, the developed method will deliver a reliable system for real-world face mask detection with strong performance characteristics. This study adds value by offering a more precise, fast, and innovative model for a mask detection system that answers the needs for overall public security.

articleTitle: An Effective Brain Tumor Segmentation and Classification Framework using Transformer-based Res-Unet++ and ShuffleNetV2
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In present generation, brain tumors are assumed as serious illnesses that lead to a high death rate. Recognizing and categorizing tumors in the brain because of the orientation, varying framework, irregular cell growth, and position is a challenging task in the field of medical image processing. Automatic classification and segmentation for detecting the presence of tumor cells are essential for preventing errors in diagnosis and maximizing the victim's rate of survival. Traditional machine learning strategy classifies tumors in the brain according to a particular characteristic chosen by a radiologist expert. It leads to an error during implementation as well as minimizes the efficiency of a strategy. Deep learning algorithms have acquired a great interest in the field of image categorization because of their effective performance in recent years. Deep learning serves as a flexible and powerful approach to resolve challenges in healthcare image evaluation, which includes, brain tumor, breast cancer, and lung cancer recognition. Automatic segmentation on huge datasets can attain improved performance by employing deep learning methods. Hence, with the support of deep learning intellectual brain tumor segmentation and classification technique is implemented in this paper. In the beginning, from the online resources, the significant images are aggregated and it is given to the Trans-Res-UNet++ (TRUNet++)-based segmentation process, where the abnormalities are segmented from the given input. Then the segmented image attained from the TRUNet++ model is fed into the ShufflenetV2 (SNetV2)-based classification process, where the tumor classification is performed. In the end, the effectiveness of the presented model is analyzed with the conventional brain tumor segmentation and classification models that guarantee the reliability and accuracy of the generated model.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Memory-Based Collaborative Filtering and Deep Learning Models for Resolving Cold Start and Data Sparsity Issues in E-commerce Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In today’s digital landscape, where online activities and e-commerce play pivotal roles, Recommender Systems (RS) have become indispensable tools for enhancing user experiences by providing personalized recommendations. However, collaborative filtering (CF) algorithms often face challenges such as the cold start problem and data sparsity. This work addresses these challenges using memory-based CF approaches such as Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), SVD++, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Baseline, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Basic. Hyperparameters for these algorithms are optimized using GridSearchCV with cross-validation values set to 5, 10, and 15. Additionally, Deep Learning (DL) models including LSTM, BiLSTM, Att+BiLSTM, User-Product Fusion (UPF), and Deep Collaborative Filtering (DCF) are explored. The BiLSTM model achieves a lower Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.1224, while the DCF model achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.6897. Among the evaluated models, SVD++ achieves an RMSE of 0.9881 and an MAE of 0.7003 with cross-validation set to 15, indicating superior predictive accuracy. The best performance is observed with cross-validation set to 15. These results highlight the effectiveness of optimized memory-based CF algorithms in overcoming the cold start and data sparsity issues, leading to more accurate and reliable recommendations. The findings suggest that memory-based CF algorithms, specifically SVD++, can significantly enhance the development of robust recommender systems, ultimately improving user experience in e-commerce and other online platforms.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Model for Accurate Road Accident Severity Classification from CCTV Footage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Road accidents threaten public safety and infrastructure enormously. A surveillance system capable of detecting and grading such accidents would speed response times by communicating such information as location crash type to rescue teams. This research paper proposes a novel scheme: a 19 level Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for the automatic detection and classification of road traffic accident severity based on its severity. With the Road Accidents from CCTV Footages Dataset, which includes four classes—no accident, severity scores 1, 2, and 3—our model learns to discern accurately whether an accident is occurring and at what level it is dangerous. This proposed CNN structure appears to be highly effective, as seen during evaluation. The training accuracy reached 98.17%, showing that it can correctly learn from the data set. Not only does validation accuracy prove its robustness in nature, but it is also accurate being a high 99.04 % on average. When tested, this further demonstrates the model's strong generalizing ability: the average test accuracy rate was as high as 98%. Furthermore, the model lends itself well to discrimination showing off a good (average Area Under the Curve value of 0.95. This tells us it is highly effective in distinguishing between different levels of accident severity) This study on Road Safety makes a contribution to enhancing automated systems for detecting accidents and rating their seriousness. The proposed CNN model's high accuracy and capacity for differentiating levels of accident severity suggests that it could in the future be used to good effect in practical emergencies, reducing fallout from road crashes.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Security Protocols for Cloud Computing Algorithms in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Cellular ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) have become increasingly popular in cell computing packages, inclusive of cellular computing, fitness care, automobile, and army packages. As such, safety protocols used in the transmission of records over MANETs are of essential importance for their hit usage. In this paper, we endorse an evaluation of safety protocols for cloud computing algorithms in MANETs. We first discuss the main safety necessities that have to be satisfied. At the same time, a cloud set of rules is adopted in a MANET and then provides a survey of different security protocols that can be used to relax the cloud algorithms for MANETs. We are aware of precise cloud algorithms for MANETs: Opportunistic Routing and Cooperative Caching. We look at the safety of these cloud algorithms under three one-of-a-kind security protocols—SSL/TLS, IPSec, and 2FA—and examine the effect of these protection protocols on their execution. Finally, we summarize our findings and offer guidelines for the adoption of security protocols in MANETs for cloud-based total computing algorithms.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN & Random Forest Model for Effective Ginger Leaf Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This study uses a method based on machine learning to conduct a thorough analysis into the automatic categorization of illnesses affecting ginger leaves. The study focuses on eight distinct classes of ginger leaf diseases: Leaf Spot (Phyllosticta zingiberi), Yellow Leaf Roll (Ginger Yellows), Leaves Blight (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides), Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum), Rhizome Rot (Pythium spp.), Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum), The powdery Mildew (Oidium spp.), and Anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.). The system of classification is evaluated using important performance indicators such as precision, recall, or F1-Score, which provide insight into the model’s capacity to accurately identify every illness class. The total number of instances for each class is indicated by the support values, ensuring a diverse as well as representative dataset for testing and training purposes. Precision ratings that range from 91.39% ability 94.44% demonstrate the model’s ability to reliably categorise each condition. Furthermore, recall rates greater than 90% highlight the model’s responsiveness in capturing cases of each disease type. The resulting F1-Score, which balances precision and recall, regularly averages 92.50%. Weighted average metrics, which account for class imbalances, show a total precision of 92.51%, validating the framework’s robustness across several disease categories. The micro average, which treats all instances equally, is consistent with the general precision, confirming the model’s dependability. According to the study, the suggested model for machine learning has a high level of reliability and generalizability. This makes it a useful tool for automated identification and categorization of ginger leaf diseases. This study advances agricultural and botanic practices by providing a realistic approach for early identification of diseases in ginger plants.

articleTitle: Cryptography: A Comparative Analysis of Symmetric and Asymmetric Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: In the modern digital environment, a wide range of crucial services and enormous amounts of sensitive data are hosted online. This paradigm includes platforms for social networking, e-commerce, cloud storage, financial transactions, and much more. To prevent unauthorized access and data theft, it is crucial to protect data during transmission. A fundamental method, called cryptography, is essential to protect data confidentiality and integrity while it travels across enormous networks. This paper examines cryptography for encoding-decoding data and performs a comparative analysis of cryptography techniques based on various parameters. The parameters include- Encryption time, Decryption time, Resistance to Quantum attacks, and Key length. We compare six different cryptography techniques-Advanced Encryption Standard(AES), Triple Data Encryption Standard(3DES), Rivert Cypher 4(RC4), Rivest-Shamir-Adelman (RSA), Elliptical Curve Cryptography (ECC), and ElGamal and analyze them. Out of all these techniques AES and ECC are found to be most suitable for the protection of data.

articleTitle: FlexIPAccess: Dynamic Attribute based IP analysis using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: With the rapid growth of cloud service adoption, ensuring efficient IP access control and reputation verification has become a critical concern. Cybersecurity engineers are currently facing complexities in managing numerous security tools simultaneously. One significant challenge is the time-intensive nature of security provider analysis tools, which can take days or even a week to provide information about IP. The FlexIPAccess is introduced as a machine learning-based solution that targets the urgent cybersecurity challenges faced in Information Technology (IT) operations. When acquiring IPs for public service hosting, it’s crucial to consider potential blacklisting to prevent unintentional acquisition of problematic IPs. Instances have occurred where a single IP serves multiple public applications, allowing cyber attackers to camouflage their malicious activities. This research prioritizes the detection of malicious activity through the analysis of IP patterns, historical data, network reachability, and geolocation. These factors are applied in a machine learning model for data processing and classification. Cloud-based IP providers like Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Ali Cloud, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Cloud providers utilize IP from various sources, making it difficult to verify authenticity and concurrent usage by other applications. The FlexIPAccess leverages key security platforms such as VirusTotal, AbuseIP, PhishingTank, AlienVault, and WHOIS Database for IP to gather essential insights, including IP addresses, Domain Name System (DNS), WHOIS records, Uniform Resource Locator (URL), and domains. In the proposed work, malicious IPs are detected from network logs. The dataset has been categorized into two types: Normal and Attack, with a total of 183,139 IPs used for the implementation. Three machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression—were implemented to detect and classify the malicious IPs.

articleTitle: Federated Learning and Cloud Integration for Enhanced Anomaly Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks using LSTM Models and Raspberry Pi Node
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) is increasingly utilized for monitoring and surveillance in various domains, including environmental monitoring, industrial automation, and healthcare. However, the sheer volume of data generated by WSN poses challenges for anomaly detection, especially in resource-constrained environments. This paper proposes a novel approach that combines federated learning and cloud integration to address the challenges of anomaly detection in WSN. Leveraging federated learning allows for collaborative model training across distributed sensor nodes while preserving data privacy. Cloud integration provides scalable computational resources for model aggregation and storage, enabling efficient anomaly detection. The implementation utilizes Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, well-suited for capturing temporal dependencies in sensor data. Raspberry Pi-based WSN nodes are employed for their low-power consumption and flexibility, enabling deployment in diverse environments. Communication between sensor nodes and the cloud is facilitated through the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol, ensuring efficient data transmission. Cloud integration is realized using Microsoft azure, offering robust cloud infrastructure for model aggregation and management. TensorFlow Federated (TFF) framework is utilized for federated learning, enabling collaborative model training across distributed nodes. Experimental evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving significant improvements in anomaly detection accuracy and efficiency. Specifically, our approach achieves up to a 20% increase in detection accuracy compared to centralized approaches. Furthermore, integrating federated learning and cloud infrastructure results in a 25% reduction in processing time, enabling real-time anomaly detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Early churn prediction in freemium game mobile using Transformer-based architecture for tabular data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This study introduces an application of the Feature Tokenizer Transformer architecture, a specialized adaptation of the well-known Transformer for tabular data, to predict early-stage churn in freemium mobile games. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of over 268,370 users, we focus on the meticulous preprocessing of minimal feature sets that are available immediately after post-tutorial phase of user’s onboarding. These features, easily collectible through any Application Data Monitoring system, include device information, user demographics, user acquisition data, user interactions during tutorial steps, and initial session behavior. We propose an novel approach for imputing missing numerical data values by developing Gradient Boosted Regression models for each individual column within the dataset. This approach is designed to understand the complexity relationship between values in columns, allowing to predict the null values accurately rather than simply filling them with mean or zero values. Despite the inherent challenges associated with the FT-Transformer, such as extensive training times, hyperparameter tuning complexities, and a substantial data requirement, our methodology achieved an Area Under ROC Curve of 94.9%, an accuracy of 86.79% and recall of 88.75%, demonstrates significant potential in enhancing churn prediction accuracy. While eXtreme Gradient Boosting currently surpasses the FT-Transformer in performance, our approach still outperforms existing methods in early churn detection for freemium mobile games. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to explore the potential of the FT-Transformer in freemium mobile game early churn detection, achieving high performance with a generalized dataset adaptable to various applications. We also introduce a machine learning-based imputation strategy for missing data, addressing a common problem in early churn prediction.

articleTitle: Bipol-Driven Bias Analysis in Transformer Models: A Quantitative, Global, and Local Interpretability Approach for Textual Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Bias in machine learning models for text data analysis can perpetuate harmful stereotypes and inequalities. This paper presents a methodology combining quantitative bias assessment, global interpretability, and local interpretability techniques to identify and understand potential biases in transformer-based text classification models. The approach collects diverse text data, encodes it using pre-trained transformers (BERT, RoBERTa), and trains neural networks to classify multiple bias types like gender, racial, and religious discrimination. The Bipol metric quantifies bias by calculating sentence-level scores based on frequencies of expert-curated bias terms across protected groups, normalized by word count. Existing Bipol axes are extended to incorporate additional bias dimensions. The SHAP (SHAPley Additive exPlanations) library provides global interpretability, validating the importance of Bipol-identified bias tokens in model decisions. Local interpretability uses Lime (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) to probe instance-level reasoning, revealing individual feature impacts on biased predictions. Corpus performance, Bipol scores, global and local explanations are combined into visualizations for holistic bias understanding. Integrating explainability libraries with Bipol enables comprehensive model analysis, auditing, and continuous improvement facilitated by external feedback. This methodology highlights the need for bias detection and interpretability, providing a transparent framework to address and mitigate biases for fair decision-making in text data applications.

articleTitle: High-Accuracy Detection of Cancer, COVID-19, and Tuberculosis in Chest CT Scans Using Fine-Tuned InceptionV3
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Revolutionizing disease diagnosis across a variety of imaging modalities have been brought on by the rapid advances in deep learning for medical image analysis. Our study introduces a novel approach to simultaneously detecting three significant diseases--cancer, COVID-19, and tuberculosis--using chest CT scans. Employing a solitary multi-class classifier, we used an optimized InceptionV3 CNN to achieve high accuracy in disease detection. For training and assessment, we employed a diverse dataset including confirmed cases of these diseases and healthy samples that were augmented for robustness. When the Chest CT dataset was used to fine-tune InceptionV3 for transfer learning, model performance improved further. Our results showed outstanding accuracy (99.43% precision) in distinguishing diseases from healthy scans. This both confirms the fidelity of the model and supports its use as a tool for diagnosis. The substantial clinical implications of this model's sensitivity and specificity allows for timely detection and best treatment of patients. By offering a precise method for recognizing critical conditions in chest CTs, this research contributes significantly to medical image processing and could lead to better healthcare outcomes and more efficient resource utilization.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality in Tourism Industry within the Framework of Virtual Reality Markup Language
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) technology has grown and emerged in the tourism industry. It offering immersive and interactive experiences, VR has transformed how people discover and interact with the VRML and people interact with different destinations. This article explores the use of VR in tourism, and focusing on Virtual Reality Markup Language (VRML) and its role in showcasing the evolution of head-mounted displays (HMDs) and the various applications of VR. It emphasizes how VR can improve travel experiences, aid in destination planning, preserve cultural heritage, support adventure tourism, and revolutionize destination marketing. The article also gives the challenges and limitations faced by VR in tourism, as well as future trends and opportunities in the field. The article impact of VR on the tourism industry and discusses the combination of Augmented Reality (AR) and VR to create virtual art exhibitions in physical and online spaces. Additionally, it provides insights into the future of VR, AR, and Mixed Reality (MR), the use of VRML, and the development of 3D modeling for creating virtual environments that help users achieve learning objectives.

articleTitle: Probability of Cancer Risk (PCR) Prediction in Adults via Dermal Intake of Groundwater using Advanced Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Groundwater contamination poses a significant public health risk, particularly in regions like Saudi Arabia where groundwater is a primary water source. This study evaluates the effectiveness of advanced machine learning (ML) models, Kernel Support Vector Machine (SVM-K), and Boosted Trees (BT), in predicting the Probability of Cancer Risk (PCR) from dermal intake of contaminated groundwater in Saudi Arabia. Using heavy metals like Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), Cadmium (Cd), and Lead (Pb) as predictors, the study compares two combinations of each model type, SVM-K (C1 and C2) and BT (C1 and C2), across several performance metrics. For SVM-k the MAPE values were extremely low, 0.1596% (C1) and 0.1429% (C2), with negligible negative PBIAS values of -0.0013 (C1) and -0.0045 (C2), suggesting highly accurate and unbiased predictions. In contrast, for BT, the MAPE values were higher at 0.9591% (C1) and 1.0214% (C2), with positive PBIAS values of 0.0401 (C1) and 0.0482 (C2), indicating a tendency to slightly overestimate PCR. The results emphasize the potential of SVM-K models in providing reliable and accurate PCR predictions, essential for effective public health interventions and groundwater management, aligning with global health and environmental sustainability goals. The integration of these findings could significantly improve the efficacy of public health advisories and targeted remediation efforts, thereby reducing the health impacts associated with contaminated groundwater.

articleTitle: Navigating the Roadblocks: Lessons Learned from a Gardening Society Conversational RAG Bot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbots hold immense potential for enhancing user engagement and information access. However, bringing such a system to life on a real-world platform presents unique challenges. This article explores the design of the chatbot, and the hurdles encountered in productionizing an LLM-RAG chatbot for a gardening society website. We delve into specific roadblocks faced during development, including•Domain-Specific Knowledge Acquisition: Training the LLM on a comprehensive gardening knowledge base proved crucial to ensure accurate and relevant responses.•Balancing Open-Endedness with Focus: While LLMs excel at open-ended conversation, enabling the chatbot to answer gardening queries effectively required focused training strategies.•Integration with Website Infrastructure: Seamless integration of the chatbot into the society's website involved addressing technical considerations and ensuring a user-friendly experience.We present the solutions implemented to overcome these challenges, offering valuable insights for those considering deploying similar LLM-RAG chatbots for niche online communities. The article concludes by discussing the lessons learned and the potential impact of such chatbots on the future of online user interactions.

articleTitle: Synergistic Approach to Refining Classification of Cutting Defects in Broad Strip Sheet Metal: CNN SVM Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The study focused on the development and evaluation of a classification model to detect various types of sheet metal defects. The dataset used in the study included instances of Wavy edges, One-sided wavy edges, Coil breaks, and Central buckles. Precision values for each defect type were as follows: Wavy edges (96.49%), One-sided wavy edges (98.22%), Coil breaks (96.95%), and Central buckles (97.72%), demonstrating the model's accuracy in identifying each defect type correctly. Recall values, which indicate the model's ability to classify instances of a class accurately, ranged from 96.46% to 98.04%. Using synergistic CNN-SVM to detect broad strip sheet metal cutting flaws, the model had 97.37% accuracy on 13,740 pictures. The F1-Score, a metric that combines precision and recall, was high for all classes, ranging from 97.09% to 97.72%. Support values provided the number of instances in each class: 3090 for Wavy edges, 3970 for One-sided wavy edges, 3570 for Coil breaks, and 3110 for Central buckles. The support proportion reflected the relative frequency of each class in the dataset, ranging from 0.22 to 0.29. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 99%, indicating the proportion of correctly classified instances across all classes. The study's results emphasized the model's strong performance in accurately detecting and classifying sheet metal defects, supported by high precision, recall, and F1-Score metrics for individual classes and aggregated averages. These findings highlight the model's potential application in industrial settings for quality control in sheet metal manufacturing, providing reliable defect detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Review on Snake Species Identification on Snake Bite Marks using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Snakebite incidents pose significant public health challenges, particularly in regions like Kaltungo, Nigeria, where identifying the snake species responsible for bites is crucial for administering proper treatment. Traditional methods relying on verbal descriptions or blood sample analysis are often inaccurate or impractical. Leveraging deep learning techniques, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), offers a promising solution for automated snake species identification from snake bite marks. This review explores the application of CNNs and Siamese Network Models for this purpose, emphasizing the need for improved datasets, model interpretability, and validation methods. The proposed methodology combines CNNs for initial feature extraction and classification with Siamese Networks for refining classification through image comparisons. By addressing challenges such as limited datasets and variable snake characteristics, this approach aims to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of snake species identification, thereby facilitating timely medical responses and ecological monitoring.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Hybrid Ensemble Approach for Image-Based Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: As increasingly sophisticated forms of malware threaten individuals, organizations, and critical systems, detection tools are becoming more important than ever. The latter, machine learning, specifically Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, and ensemble learning, were applied for malware detection to a dataset consisting of more than 9000 malware samples from the Malevis dataset. That is the SVM resulted in an accuracy of 89% while the RF showed an even more superior accuracy of 93% thereby indicating it to be quite an effective model for the purpose of malware classification. And it was worth noting that the accuracy reached 92.6% on VotingClassifier ensemble, which provided a great boost- for example, to Allaple and Expiro. This study supports the potential for combining different machine learning classifiers and the utility of feature extraction from different image-based methods in order to achieve effective malware detection.

articleTitle: Detection of Alzheimer's Disease from 2D MRI Data using LeNet Extension with Dropout
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) stands as a serious issue in today’s health scenario. Among the affected brain regions, the hippocampus stands out and serves as a readily accessible biomarker through MRI images. While employing whole MRI images has shown decreased accuracy in Alzheimer’s classification within machine learning, our paper introduces the select slice technique and focuses on areas within the various regions of MRI images. The investigation aims to identify which MRI image viewpoints yield superior accuracy in AD detection. To evaluate the efficacy of viewpoints and perspective, utilizing the publicly accessible Kaggle dataset, employing Pre-trained ResNet and LeNet architectures. Our analysis encompassed a total of 5200 MRI images across axial, coronal and sagittal. These model findings demonstrate that selecting specific slices outperforms the use of entire MRI slices for AD classification. Notably, our approach enhances machine learning accuracy, with the coronal view exhibiting particularly high accuracy. This methodology significantly contributes to improving machine learning performance in AD classification, with results aligning closely with those of medical experts commonly engaged in AD diagnosis and observed that accuracy is 99.7 percent, suggesting that LeNet models hold promise as effective tools for AD classification.

articleTitle: Optimizing Hyderabad's Carbon Footprint: A Machine Learning Approach for Smart City Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate Hyderabad City's progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 11, which aims to make urban areas more welcoming, secure, resilient, and environmentally friendly for all people. More than half of humanity now resides in urban areas. Roughly seven out of ten individuals will call an urban region home by the year 2050. With its potential to become India's IT and financial capital and home to the country's defence and missile research centre, Hyderabad is already a large city. However, in the past two years, the city's reputation as an ideal location for startups and investors has spread around the globe. This is due to its robust ecosystem and logical support, and predictions indicate that it will become a megacity and global leader in IT by 2030, with further growth expected until 2050. So, in order to ensure the city's sustainable development, In this paper, we will take a look at the city's carbon emissions from the past and look forward to what the future holds. We'll also make some predictions about sustainable development, like how the city's roads and transport will be improved to make it more resilient and eco-friendlier. The study used data from the city of Hyderabad from 1993 to 2019 to calculate emissions and create a carbon estimate dataset for the transport sector from 2002 to 2019. It also forecasted vehicle growth and carbon estimates up to 2030.

articleTitle: Fracture Forecasting through Deep Learning's Role in Bone Injury Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The primary objective of this research is to investigate the critical issue of finding and classifying bone fractures through the application of advanced image analysis techniques. Because bone fractures are so common and have such a significant influence on the outcomes of patients, it is essential that they be detected in a timely manner through adequate treatment. It is essential to identify abnormalities as soon as possible in order to reduce their impact and maximise overall recovery. A dataset consisting of 4906 X-ray images is utilised for the study. These images are divided into two categories: fractured and non-fractured respectively. The Sequential Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is utilised in this algorithm. The CNN model is able to attain an astounding accuracy of 98% in fracture classification by utilising a training set of 4099 photographs, a testing set of 401 photographs, and an additional 406 photographs for validation. Deep learning in medical imaging is demonstrated to be capable of providing accurate and efficient fracture diagnosis through the use of this technology, which demonstrates the potential of this approach to enhance the outcomes of healthcare.

articleTitle: Cancer Detection: Detecting cancer using ultrasound by Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Cancer is one of the major leading causes of death worldwide despite several advancements in the field of technology and medical science. The detection of cancer, especially in its early stages, is proven to be very beneficial for the recovery of the patient. However, the process often involves complex procedures and requires skilled medical professionals, making the costly cure challenging to reach remote places and poor population. In light of these challenges, there is an increasing demand for efficient and accessible diagnostic tools. This is where our proposed model comes into use. Leveraging deep learning techniques, our model basically performs the tasks below: detecting whether the image is ultrasound or not, classifying the organ present in ultrasound images, breast cancer detection, and gallbladder cancer detection. These models align with the need for accurate and fast cancer detection, which can significantly improve patient survival chances. For detecting ultrasound or not as well as organ classification, the ResNet50 model is used which identifies the ultrasound images, and accurately classifies them based on the organ they represent. This capability is crucial in determining the appropriate treatment plan for patients. The model further enhances its utility by identifying whether the breast image has any cancer or not using a VGG16 model. This feature is crucial in early detection and prevention of breast cancer. At last, the model incorporates gallbladder cancer detection using another ResNet50 model. Early detection of these diseases can significantly improve patient survival chances. The approach lowers the need for manual inspection by automating these operations, improving healthcare delivery's accuracy and efficiency. In addition, it offers a platform for ongoing education and development, advancing medical technology.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Perspective on Skin Cancer Classification: Insights from Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Skin cancer detection is a critical aspect of dermatological practice, requiring the timely and accurate differentiation of benign and malignant lesions. In this research, we explore the usefulness of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for automating the classification of skin cancer, with an emphasis on the binary difference between benign and malignant lesions. Scaling, normalization, and augmentation techniques were used to meticulously compile a comprehensive dataset of dermatoscopic images from reputable medical archives and dermatological databases to enhance model robustness and generalization. Metrics for both training and validation were monitored concurrently throughout the iterative training of the CNN model across several epochs. Our findings indicate that training and validation loss reduce steadily throughout epochs, indicating that the model progressively improves its ability to lower prediction inaccuracy. Simultaneously, accuracy increases consistently, demonstrating CNN's competence in accurately categorizing skin lesions. After 55 epochs, the model culminates at 0.97, a notable accuracy. Validation measurements, where validation accuracy achieves a maximum of 0.83 over many epochs, provide further evidence for the stability of the model. These findings demonstrate CNNs' potential as formidable instruments for automated skin cancer identification, opening doors for improved precision and efficacy in therapeutic contexts. Additional research is required to optimize and refine CNN-based methods for practical use in the diagnosis and classification of skin cancer.

articleTitle: SemConv: Deep Learning for Emotion Decoding in Autism Individuals using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This research addresses advancements in medical decision support systems aimed at overcoming challenges in neuroscience, specifically for individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder. This technology utilizes the convolution neural network for efficiently analyzing the neural activities of individuals suffering from ASD (Autism Spectrum Disorder), which is a functional disorder occurring due to neural oscillatory malfunctioning. The proposed technology will work to detect the EEG signals in ASD individuals. Applying learned filters can be able to analyze and inspect the part of the EEG spectrum that is being utilized for reading and decoding the emotions [1]. The range of band suppression present in ASD individuals is in 2 categories – α (high) and β (high). The highα (9-13 Hz) and highβ (13-30 Hz). The deep learning model is trained using the dataset training with validation and tracking accuracy. The model consists of multiple dense layers – ReLU and dropout layer [2] which complies with the dataset using the optimizer function and sparse categorical cross-entropy loss. The evaluation will select the random EEG data sample, predict its emotion label and plot EEG data from the selected sample for visualizations. The results align with existing neuroscientific findings on emotion recognition in individuals with behavioral deficits, demonstrating that the system maintains high performance and accuracy while enhancing interpretability.

articleTitle: An Improved Approach to Classify Plant Disease using CNN and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: The recognizable proof of plant sickness utilizing a leaf test has been one of the principal subjects of review for various scientists on the grounds that to the extending uses of profound learning in different areas. This study proposes a clever half breed technique that joins the CNN AlexNet design with Irregular Backwoods to distinguish illnesses all the more precisely and with less computational exertion. The review used the proposed model to recognize sicknesses in tomatoes, potatoes, and ringer peppers utilizing information from the Plant Village dataset; the model created a f1-score of 0.9892 and a precision pace of 99.68%. A sum of 77221 pictures, circulated across 55894 pictures for preparing and 21327 pictures for approval and testing, isolated across 15 classes, were utilized for the proposed model out of the 1,75,734 pictures in the dataset, which was ordered into 38 classifications relating to different plant species and their sicknesses.

articleTitle: Enhancing Algorithmic Trading Strategies with Sentiment Analysis: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This paper discusses the application of deep reinforcement learning algorithms in stock trading, where the stock market environment is highly dynamic in nature. To represent the dynamics of the stock market, news headlines are a key factor in order to predict whether the market direction is bullish (upward) or bearish (downward). So we use different sentiment analysis models like Finbert and Roberta to see how the sentiment scores given by these models affect our trading agent’s strategy. These sentiment scores are added to our custom trading environment, where we combine these scores as part of the state along with other parameters like open, high, low, close prices and trading volume.Then for the reinforcement learning part, we used various policy gradient methods like Advantage Actor Critic (A2C), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Deep Q-Network (DQN) to train our agent in this custom environment. These models were then back-tested on historic data, where the trading strategies devised by these deep RL agents during the training phase were applied. The results provided by these models were very promising. The evaluation metrics used were the Sharpe score and Sortino score. The highest Sharpe ratio was given by the PPO agent, which was 3.0 for Facebook data and 2.834 for Goldman Sachs data, using the Roberta sentiment model. Whereas for the Finbert model, PPO got 3.24 for Facebook data and 3.03 for Goldman Sachs data. This explains that the trading portfolio is performing really well.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Feature Selection in Supervised and Unsupervised Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: Feature selection plays a pivotal role in enhancing machine learning model performance by removing irrelevant and redundant data, thus reducing dimensionality and improving computational efficiency. There are various Feature selection techniques in both supervised and unsupervised approaches. This study investigates about the performance of various base classifiers and clustering models using different feature selection techniques. This study is based on spam dataset which consist of spam emails and how feature selection makes a impact on the model. The unique aspect of our approach is trying various combinations of feature selection on the dataset and observe the results. This study also focuses on univariate and bivariate feature selection strategies and their outcomes in both supervised and unsupervised approaches. The feature selection techniques used in this study are chi-square, anova, PCA and their combinations.

articleTitle: Wearable Technology: A Machine Learning Approach for Stress, Sleep Apnea, and Atrial Fibrillation Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
abstract: This project explores the symbiotic relationship between wearable technology, machine learning, and healthcare in predicting multiple diseases through smartwatch data analysis. Concentrating on sleep apnea, atrial fibrillation (AFib), and stress detection, three predictive models were developed, achieving respective accuracies of 85%, 97%, and 87%. This research highlights how useful smartwatches can be, as they come with sensors that can monitor your heart rate, blood pressure, physical activities, and also sleep patterns in real-time, offering valuable health monitoring features. By addressing prevalent global diseases, the research highlights the projected adoption surge of wearables, exceeding one billion by 2022, and introduces an interactive interface facilitating user-input health metrics for disease prediction. The practical application of these models for consistent, real-time health checkups is emphasized. However, the study acknowledges privacy concerns and underscores the necessity for validation studies to ensure reliability. This research marks a significant stride in advancing personalized healthcare, showcasing the potential of integrating smartwatches and machine learning for proactive disease identification and prevention. The achieved accuracies of the models affirm their utility in offering tailored health insights, underscoring the transformative impact of this interdisciplinary approach on future healthcare paradigms
